title.raw: 卷27 穆崇 Volume 27: Mu Chong

sentences.zh: 穆崇，代人也。

translations.literal: Mu Chong
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Mu Chong

sentences.zh: 其先世效節於神元、桓、穆之時。

translations.literal: His forebears for generations showed loyal service in the ages of Emperor Shenyuan and the Huan and Mu emperors.
translations.idiomatic: His line had served with loyalty since the reigns of Emperor Shenyuan and the Huan and Mu emperors.

sentences.zh: 崇機捷便辟，少以盜竊為事。

translations.literal: Chong was nimble and quick-witted; in youth he made theft his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was sharp and agile; in his youth he lived by theft.

sentences.zh: 太祖之居獨孤部，崇常往來奉給，時人無及者。

translations.literal: When Taizu dwelt in the Dugu tribe, Chong constantly came and went supplying him—no one of the time could match it.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizu stayed with the Dugu tribe, Chong went back and forth to provision him as no one else could.

sentences.zh: 後劉顯之謀逆也，平文皇帝外孫梁眷知之，密遣崇告太祖。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Xian plotted rebellion, Emperor Pingwen's maternal grandson Liang Juan learned of it and secretly sent Chong to inform Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Xian plotted treason, Liang Juan—Emperor Pingwen's grandson by a daughter—learned of the plot and secretly sent Chong to warn Taizu.

sentences.zh: 眷謂崇曰：「顯若知之問汝者，丈夫當死節，雖刀劍別割，勿泄也。

translations.literal: Juan said to Chong: "If Xian learns of it and questions you, a man should die for principle; though swords cut and carve you apart, do not reveal it.
translations.idiomatic: Juan told Chong, "If Xian finds out and questions you, a man must die for his lord; let them cut you with swords—do not speak.

sentences.zh: 」因以寵妻及所乘良馬付崇曰：「事覺，吾當以此自明。

translations.literal: " He therefore gave Chong his favored wife and the fine horse he rode, saying, "If the matter is exposed, I shall use these to clear myself.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Chong his favorite wife and his best horse, saying, "If we are found out, I will clear myself with these."

sentences.zh: 」崇來告難，太祖馳如賀蘭部。

translations.literal: " Chong came to report the peril; Taizu galloped to the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Chong brought word of danger; Taizu galloped to the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 顯果疑眷泄其謀，將囚之。

translations.literal: Xian indeed suspected Juan had leaked the plot and was about to imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian indeed suspected Juan had betrayed the plot and was about to seize him.

sentences.zh: 崇乃唱言曰：「梁眷不顧恩義，奬顯為逆，今我掠得其妻馬，足以雪忿。

translations.literal: Chong then proclaimed aloud: "Liang Juan has forgotten grace and righteousness and would back Xian in rebellion; today I have seized his wife and horse—enough to settle the score.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then shouted aloud, "Liang Juan has forgotten grace and would make Xian rebel! I have taken his wife and horse—that settles the score."

sentences.zh: 」顯聞而信之。

translations.literal: " Xian heard and believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian heard him and believed it.

sentences.zh: 窟咄之難，崇外甥于桓等謀執太祖以應之，[1]告崇曰：「今窟咄已立，眾咸歸附，富貴不可失，願舅圖之。

translations.literal: In Kudou's turmoil, Chong's sister's son Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu in collusion;[1] they told Chong: "Kudou is already established, the masses all submit—wealth and rank must not be missed; I beg you, uncle, to plan for it.
translations.idiomatic: During Kudou's revolt, Chong's nephew Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu in collusion;[1] they told Chong, "Kudou already holds the throne and all men rally to him—fortune like this is not to be lost. Uncle, we beg you to join us."

sentences.zh: 」崇乃夜告太祖，太祖誅桓等，北踰陰山，復幸賀蘭部。

translations.literal: " Chong then by night informed Taizu; Taizu executed Huan and the rest, crossed north over the Yin Mountains, and again came in fortune to the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Chong warned Taizu by night; Taizu executed Huan and his fellows, crossed the Yin Mountains to the north, and again took refuge with the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 崇甚見寵待。

translations.literal: Chong was greatly favored and treated with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Chong stood in the highest favor.

sentences.zh: 太祖為魏王，拜崇征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu became Prince of Wei, Chong was appointed General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was made Prince of Wei, Chong received the rank of General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 從平中原，賜爵歷陽公，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the Central Plains and was granted the title Duke of Liyang and made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He marched in the pacification of the Central Plains and was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang with the post of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 後遷太尉，加侍中，徙為安邑公。

translations.literal: Later he was moved to Grand Commandant, added Palace Attendant, and transferred to Duke of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Grand Commandant, given the added title of palace attendant, and advanced to Duke of Anyi.

sentences.zh: 又從征高車，大勝而還。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against the Gaoche and returned with a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against the Gaoche and came back in triumph.

sentences.zh: 姚興圍洛陽，司馬德宗將辛恭靖請救，太祖遣崇六千騎赴之。

translations.literal: Yao Xing besieged Luoyang; Sima Dezong's general Xin Gongjing requested rescue, and Taizu sent Chong with six thousand horse to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing besieged Luoyang, Xin Gongjing, general under Sima Dezong, begged for relief; Taizu sent Chong with six thousand riders.

sentences.zh: 未至，恭靖敗，詔崇即鎮野王，除豫州刺史，仍本將軍。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Gongjing was defeated; an edict ordered Chong to garrison Ye at once, made him Inspector of Yuzhou, and he retained his former general's rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had not yet arrived when Gongjing fell; an edict set him to garrison Ye immediately, named him inspector of Yuzhou, and left him his former general's rank.

sentences.zh: 徵為太尉，又徙宜都公。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Commandant and again transferred to Duke of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to Grand Commandant and again advanced to Duke of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 天賜三年薨。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianci he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Tianci.

sentences.zh: 先是，衞王儀謀逆，崇豫焉，太祖惜其功而祕之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince Wei Yi plotted rebellion, Chong took part beforehand; Taizu, cherishing his merit, kept it secret.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince Wei Yi plotted treason, Chong had been party to it; Taizu, valuing his service, concealed the matter.

sentences.zh: 及有司奏諡，太祖親覽諡法，至述義不克曰「丁」。

translations.literal: When the responsible offices memorialized on the posthumous name, Taizu personally reviewed the posthumous statutes; at "Unable to Fulfill Righteous Intent" the syllable was "Ding."
translations.idiomatic: When the offices submitted a posthumous name, Taizu read the statutes himself; at the entry "Unable to Fulfill Righteous Intent" he came to the syllable Ding.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此當矣。

translations.literal: Taizu said: "This fits.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "That is the one."

sentences.zh: 」乃諡曰丁公。

translations.literal: " He therefore gave the posthumous title Lord Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore posthumously named him Lord Ding.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖避窟咄之難，遣崇還察人心。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Taizu fled Kudou's turmoil, he sent Chong back to observe men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, fleeing Kudou's revolt, Taizu had sent Chong back to gauge where loyalties lay.

sentences.zh: 崇夜至民中，留馬與從者，乃微服入其營。

translations.literal: Chong came at night among the people, left his horse with attendants, and in plain dress entered their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Chong reached the camps by night, left his horse with his men, and went in disguised.

sentences.zh: 會有火光，為舂妾所識，賊皆驚起。

translations.literal: There happened to be firelight; a woman pounding grain recognized him, and the bandits all sprang up in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Firelight betrayed him; a woman at the mortar recognized him, and the rebels leapt up in alarm.

sentences.zh: 崇求從者不得，因匿於坑中，徐乃竊馬奔走。

translations.literal: Chong could not find his attendants; he hid in a pit, then slowly stole a horse and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find his men, he hid in a pit, then slowly stole a horse and fled.

sentences.zh: 宿於大澤，有白狼向崇而號，崇乃覺悟，馳馬隨狼而走。

translations.literal: He lodged in the great marsh; a white wolf came toward Chong and howled; Chong took warning, galloped after the wolf, and thus escaped peril.
translations.idiomatic: He spent the night in a great marsh; a white wolf howled at him; taking it as a sign, he galloped after the wolf and escaped.

sentences.zh: 適去，賊黨追者已至，遂得免難。

translations.literal: He had just gone when the pursuers of the rebel band arrived, and so he escaped danger.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely gone when the rebel pursuers arrived; thus he slipped free.

sentences.zh: 太祖異之，命崇立祀，子孫世奉焉。

translations.literal: Taizu marveled at it and ordered Chong to establish a shrine; descendants for generations have offered sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu marveled and ordered a shrine to Chong; descendants have sacrificed there ever since.

sentences.zh: 太和中，追錄功臣，以崇配饗。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, when meritorious subjects were recorded, Chong was granted joint sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taihe court recorded founding merit, Chong was admitted to joint sacrifice at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 崇長子遂留，歷顯官。

translations.literal: Chong's eldest son Suiliu held distinguished offices through the years.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's eldest son Suiliu rose through a series of high posts.

sentences.zh: 討蠕蠕有功，賜爵零陵侯。

translations.literal: In campaigning against the Rouran he had merit and was granted Marquis of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: For merit against the Rouran he was enfeoffed Marquis of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 後以罪廢。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for crime.
translations.idiomatic: He was later stripped of rank for a crime.

sentences.zh: 子乙九，內行長者。

translations.literal: His son Yijiu was a man of mature conduct within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yijiu was esteemed within the palace for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵富城公，加建忠將軍，遷散騎常侍、內乘黃令、侍中。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Duke of Fucheng, made General Who Establishes Loyalty, and moved to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bearer of the Imperial Household Yellow Gate, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Fucheng and named General Who Establishes Loyalty, then rose to cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, bearer of the imperial household yellow gate, and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰靜。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 子真，起家中散，轉侍東宮，尚長城公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Zhen began his career as Central Scribe, was transferred to attend the Eastern Palace, married the Princess of Changcheng, and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen began as central scribe, was moved to attend the heir apparent, married the Princess of Changcheng, and became commandant of cavalry escort.

sentences.zh: 後敕離婚，納文明太后姊。

translations.literal: Later an edict ordered divorce; he took the elder sister of Empress Dowager Wenming.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict forced divorce; he married Empress Dowager Wenming's elder sister.

sentences.zh: 尋除南部尚書、侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Southern Department Minister and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named southern department minister and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖追思崇勳，令著作郎韓顯宗與真撰定碑文，建於白登山。

translations.literal: Gaozu, recalling Chong's merit, ordered Compiler Han Xianzong and Zhen together to fix the text of a stele and erect it on Mount Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, remembering Chong's service, ordered Han Xianzong of the compilation bureau and Zhen to draft a stele and set it up on Mount Bai.

sentences.zh: 真子泰，本名石洛，高祖賜名焉。

translations.literal: Zhen's son Tai, original name Shiluo, was given his present name by Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's son Tai, originally named Shiluo, received his new name from Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子孫，尚章武長公主，拜駙馬都尉，典羽獵四曹事，賜爵馮翊侯。

translations.literal: As a meritorious descendant he married the Princess of Zhangwu Chang, was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort, put in charge of the Four Bureaus of the Imperial Hunt, and granted Marquis of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious scion he married the Princess of Zhangwu Chang, became commandant of cavalry escort, oversaw the four bureaus of the imperial hunt, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中尚書，加散騎常侍、安西將軍。

translations.literal: He was moved to Palace Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat and added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Stabilizes the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace supervisor of the imperial secretariat with the added titles of cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and general who stabilizes the west.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised from marquis to duke.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮南將軍、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Stabilizes the South and Governor of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as general who stabilizes the south and governor of Luo.

sentences.zh: 例降為侯。

translations.literal: By precedent his rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Under standing rules he stepped down one grade to marquis.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為右光祿大夫、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as right grand master for splendid happiness and right vice director of the imperial secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又出為使持節、鎮北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: He again went out as Bearer of Staff with Full Powers, General Who Stabilizes the North, and Governor of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He went out again as bearer of staff with full powers, general who stabilizes the north, and governor of Ding.

sentences.zh: 改封馮翊縣開國侯，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Fengyi, state-founding, with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to state-founding Marquis of Fengyi with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進征北將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Campaigns North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who campaigns north.

sentences.zh: 初，文明太后幽高祖於別室，將謀黜廢，泰切諫乃止。

translations.literal: At first Empress Dowager Wenming had confined Gaozu in a separate chamber and was about to plot deposition and removal; Tai remonstrated sharply and she stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Wenming first confined Gaozu apart and plotted to depose him, Tai remonstrated fiercely and she desisted.

sentences.zh: 高祖德之，錫以山河，寵待隆至。

translations.literal: Gaozu was grateful for his virtue and therefore bestowed on him mountains-and-rivers reward, favoring him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu owed him gratitude, granted him the mountains-and-rivers reward, and favored him to the summit.

sentences.zh: 泰自陳病久，乞為恒州，遂轉陸叡為定州，以泰代焉。

translations.literal: Tai himself reported long illness and begged for Heng Province; Lu Rui was therefore transferred to Ding Province and Tai took his place.
translations.idiomatic: Tai pleaded chronic illness and asked for Heng Province; Lu Rui was moved to Ding and Tai replaced him.

sentences.zh: 泰不願遷都，叡未及發而泰已至，遂濳相扇誘，圖為叛。

translations.literal: Tai did not wish to see the capital moved; before Rui could set out Tai had already arrived, and they secretly incited one another, plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to see the capital moved, Tai reached his post before Rui could depart; the two secretly stirred each other toward rebellion.

sentences.zh: 乃與叡及安樂侯元隆，撫冥鎮將、魯郡侯元業，驍騎將軍元超，陽平侯賀頭，射聲校尉元樂平，前彭城鎮將元拔，代郡太守元珍，鎮北將軍、樂陵王思譽等謀推朔州刺史陽平王頤為主。

translations.literal: He then with Rui and Marquis of Anle Yuan Long, Garrison Commander of Fuming and Marquis of Lu Commandery Yuan Ye, Valiant Cavalry General Yuan Chao, Marquis of Yangping He Tou, Commandant of Archers Who Shoot at Sound Yuan Yueping, former Garrison Commander of Pengcheng Yuan Ba, Administrator of Dai Commandery Yuan Zhen, General Who Stabilizes the North and Prince of Leling Siyu, and others plotted to set up Yi, Prince of Yangping and Inspector of Shuozhou, as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Rui, Yuan Long Marquis of Anle, Yuan Ye garrison commander of Fuming and Marquis of Lu, Yuan Chao valiant cavalry general, He Tou Marquis of Yangping, Yuan Yueping commandant of archers who shoot at sound, Yuan Ba former garrison commander of Pengcheng, Yuan Zhen administrator of Dai, Siyu general who stabilizes the north and Prince of Leling, and others to make Yi, Prince of Yangping in Shuozhou, their sovereign.

sentences.zh: 頤不從，偽許以安之，密表其事。

translations.literal: Yi did not follow them; he falsely assented to calm them and secretly memorialized the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yi would not join them; he feigned assent to quiet them and reported the plot in a secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃遣任城王澄率并肆兵以討之。

translations.literal: Gaozu then sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng to raise Bing and Si troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Prince Cheng of Rencheng with troops from Bing and Si to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 澄先遣治書侍御史李煥單車入代，出其不意，泰等驚駭，計無所出。

translations.literal: Cheng first sent Attendant-in-Ordinary who Investigates Documents Li Huan alone on horseback into Dai, taking them unawares; Tai and the rest were alarmed and had no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng first sent Li Huan, attendant-in-ordinary who investigates documents, alone on horseback into Dai to catch them off guard; Tai and his party were thrown into panic with no plan left.

sentences.zh: 煥曉諭逆徒，示以禍福，於是凶黨離心，莫為之用。

translations.literal: Huan enlightened the rebels with gain and loss, showing fortune and calamity; the wicked party lost heart and none would serve them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan explained fortune and ruin to the rebels; the plotters lost heart and none would fight for them.

sentences.zh: 泰自度必敗，乃率麾下數百人攻煥郭門，冀以一捷。

translations.literal: Tai judged he must fail and led his followers—several hundred men—to attack Huan at the outer gate, hoping for one victory.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing defeat inevitable, Tai led several hundred men against Huan at the outer gate, hoping for a single stroke of luck.

sentences.zh: 不克，單馬走出城西，為人擒送。

translations.literal: He could not take it; alone on horseback he fled out the west gate and was seized and sent in.
translations.idiomatic: He failed, fled alone through the west gate, was captured, and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 澄亦尋到，窮治黨與。

translations.literal: Cheng also soon arrived and thoroughly prosecuted the party.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng arrived soon after and prosecuted the conspiracy to the end.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸代，親見罪人，問其反狀，泰等伏誅。

translations.literal: Gaozu came to Dai, personally saw the culprits, questioned them on their rebellion, and Tai and the rest were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu came to Dai, questioned the rebels himself, and Tai and his fellows were executed.

sentences.zh: 子伯智，八歲侍學東宮，十歲拜太子洗馬、散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Bozhi, at eight sui attended study in the Eastern Palace; at ten he was made Palace Groom and Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozhi entered the Eastern Palace school at eight; at ten he was made palace groom and supernumerary cavalier attendant.

sentences.zh: 尚饒陽公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Raoyang and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Raoyang and became commandant of cavalry escort.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died before his time.

sentences.zh: 子喈。

translations.literal: His son Jie.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jie.

sentences.zh: 伯智弟士儒，字叔賢。

translations.literal: Bozhi's younger brother Shiru, style name Shuxian.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi's younger brother Shiru, styled Shuxian.

sentences.zh: 徙涼州，後乃得還。

translations.literal: He was moved to Liang Province; only later was he able to return.
translations.idiomatic: He was relocated to Liang Province and was able to return only later.

sentences.zh: 為太尉參軍事。

translations.literal: He was made aide to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as aide to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 子容，武定中，汲郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Rong, in the Wuding era, was Administrator of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rong was administrator of Ji commandery in the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 乙九弟忸頭，侍中、北部尚書。

translations.literal: Yijiu's younger brother Niutou was Palace Attendant and Northern Department Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yijiu's younger brother Niutou served as palace attendant and northern department minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Lord of Works and given posthumous name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named lord of works with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 子蒲坂，虞曹尚書、征虜將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Puban was Minister of the Imperial Stud, General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, and Inspector of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Puban was minister of the imperial stud, general who campaigns against the barbarians, and inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 贈征西將軍、雍州刺史，諡曰昭。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Yong; posthumous name Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named general who campaigns west and inspector of Yong, with the posthumous title Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子韶，字伏興，員外散騎侍郎、代郡太守、征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Shao, style name Fuxing, was Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, Administrator of Dai Commandery, General Who Campaigns East, and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao, styled Fuxing, was supernumerary cavalier attendant, administrator of Dai commandery, general who campaigns east, and grand master for splendid happiness with golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈使持節、都督冀相殷三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、冀州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Bearer of Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs of Ji, Xiang, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and Inspector of Ji; posthumous name Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named bearer of staff, commander of Ji, Xiang, and Yin military affairs, grand general of agile cavalry, and inspector of Ji, with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子遵伯，幽州司馬。

translations.literal: His son Zunbo was Administrator of You province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zunbo was administrator of You province.

sentences.zh: 遂留弟觀，字闥拔，襲崇爵。

translations.literal: Suiliu's younger brother Guan, style name Tabo, inherited Chong's title.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliu's younger brother Guan, styled Tabo, inherited Chong's title.

sentences.zh: 少以文藝知名，選充內侍，太祖器之。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed for literary accomplishment; he was chosen to fill the inner attendants, and Taizu valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was known for literary talent; chosen as inner attendant, he won Taizu's regard.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，為左衞將軍，綰門下中書，出納詔命。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he was made Left General of the Guard, managed the Gate and Secretariat, and issued edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he was named left general of the guard, oversaw the gate and secretariat, and issued edicts.

sentences.zh: 及訪舊事，未嘗有所遺漏，太宗奇之。

translations.literal: When he inquired into old affairs, never was anything lost; Taizong marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: When he traced precedents, no detail ever slipped; Taizong marveled.

sentences.zh: 尚宜陽公主，拜駙馬都尉，稍遷太尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Yiyang and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort, then gradually advanced to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Yiyang, became commandant of cavalry escort, and rose step by step to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 世祖之監國，觀為右弼，出則統攝朝政，入則應對左右，事無巨細，皆關決焉。

translations.literal: When Shizu supervised the state, Guan was his right-hand aide; going out he commanded the court, coming in he answered at the ruler's side—nothing great or small did not pass through his decision.
translations.idiomatic: While Shizu supervised the realm, Guan was his right hand: abroad he directed government, at court he answered the heir—nothing large or small escaped his judgment.

sentences.zh: 終日怡怡，無慍喜之色。

translations.literal: All day he was cheerful, without anger or joy on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He remained cheerful all day, never showing anger or elation on his face.

sentences.zh: 勞謙善誘，不以富貴驕人。

translations.literal: He toiled, was modest, and skillfully guided others, not arrogant because of wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: He worked hard, stayed modest, and guided others well, never arrogant in wealth or rank.

sentences.zh: 泰常八年，暴疾薨於苑內，時年三十五。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taichang he died suddenly of illness in the park, age thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Taichang he died suddenly of illness in the park at thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 太宗親臨其喪，悲慟左右。

translations.literal: Taizong came in person to his funeral and grieved so that those beside him were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong attended his funeral in person and grieved until those around him wept.

sentences.zh: 賜以通身隱起金飾棺，喪禮一依安城王叔孫俊故事。

translations.literal: He was granted a coffin of gold with hidden relief over the whole body; funeral rites followed entirely the precedent of Prince of Ancheng Shu Sun Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a coffin of gold with relief over the whole body; rites followed the precedent of Prince Shu Sun Jun of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 贈宜都王，諡曰文成。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prince of Yidu with posthumous title Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Prince of Yidu with the title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，每與羣臣談宴，未嘗不歎惜殷勤，以為自泰常以來，佐命勳臣文武兼濟無及之者，見稱如此。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, whenever he talked and feasted with the ministers he never failed to sigh with earnest praise, thinking that since Taichang there had been no founding minister combining civil and military like him—such was the praise he received.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu took the throne he never feasted with his ministers without sighing in praise, saying that since Taichang no founding minister had matched Guan's civil and military gifts—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 子壽，襲爵，少以父任選侍東宮。

translations.literal: His son Shou inherited the title; in youth, through his father's position, he was chosen to attend the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shou inherited the title and, through his father's standing, was chosen in youth to attend the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 尚樂陵公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Leling and was made Commandant of Cavalry Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Leling and became commandant of cavalry escort.

sentences.zh: 明敏有父風，世祖愛重之，擢為下大夫。

translations.literal: Bright and keen, he had his father's manner; Shizu cherished and valued him and promoted him to Lower Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and sharp, he had his father's bearing; Shizu cherished him and promoted him to lower grand master.

sentences.zh: 敷奏機辯，有聲內外。

translations.literal: In memorials and debate he was quick and had a voice within and without the court.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials and debate were nimble, and his reputation rang inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中、中書監，領南部尚書，進爵宜都王，加征東大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat, held concurrent Southern Master of Writing, advanced to Prince of Yidu, and given the additional rank General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant and director of the secretariat, took the southern master of writing, was raised to Prince of Yidu, and named general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 壽辭曰：「臣祖崇，先皇之世，屬值艱危，幸天贊梁眷，誠心密告，故得效功前朝，流福於後。

translations.literal: Shou declined, saying, "My grandfather Chong, in the former emperor's age, met hardship and peril again and again. Heaven favored Liang Juan's loyal secret warning, and so he could build merit for the earlier court and leave blessing for those after.
translations.idiomatic: Shou declined, saying, "My grandfather Chong, in the former emperor's day, met danger again and again. Heaven favored Liang Juan's loyal warning, so he served the earlier reign and left blessing for later generations.

sentences.zh: 昔陳平受賞，歸功無知，今眷元勳未錄，而臣獨弈世受榮，豈惟仰愧古賢，抑亦有虧國典。

translations.literal: In antiquity Chen Ping received reward yet attributed the merit to one without knowledge. Now Juan's founding merit is unrecorded while I alone through generations receive glory—is this not to look up ashamed before the ancient worthies and also to harm the state's statutes?
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Chen Ping took reward yet credited one who knew nothing. Yet Juan's founding service goes unrecorded while I alone inherit glory age after age—should I not blush before the ancients and breach the state's law?

sentences.zh: 」世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor Shizu praised this.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shizu praised him.

sentences.zh: 乃求眷後，得其孫，賜爵郡公。

translations.literal: He then sought Juan's descendants, found his grandson, and granted him the rank of commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out Juan's grandson and enfeoffed him duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 輿駕征涼州，命壽輔恭宗，總錄要機，內外聽焉。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned on Liang Province he ordered Shou to assist Gongzong and oversee all critical affairs; within and without all obeyed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liangzhou campaign the emperor ordered Shou to assist Gongzong and control all confidential affairs; the whole court obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 行次雲中，將濟河，宴諸將於宮。

translations.literal: Halting at Yunzhong, about to cross the river, he feasted the generals in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhong, before crossing the river, he feasted his generals in the palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖別御靜室，召壽及司徒崔浩、尚書李順，世祖謂壽曰：「蠕蠕吳提與牧犍連和，今聞朕征涼州，必來犯塞，若伏兵漠南，殄之為易。

translations.literal: The Emperor Shizu separately took the quiet chamber and summoned Shou, Minister of Education Cui Hao, and Master of Writing Li Shun. The Emperor Shizu told Shou, "Rouran's Wuti has joined with Mujian in alliance; now hearing that I campaign on Liangzhou he is sure to come violate the border. If we set ambush south of the desert, destroying them will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu withdrew to a quiet room and summoned Shou, Minister Cui Hao, and Li Shun of the masters of writing, telling Shou, "Wuti of the Rouran has allied with Mujian; hearing that I march on Liangzhou he will surely raid the frontier. Ambush him south of the desert and destruction will be easy.

sentences.zh: 朕故留壯兵肥馬，使卿輔佐太子。

translations.literal: I therefore leave strong troops and fat horses and make you assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: I have left strong troops and fat horses so that you may assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 收田既訖，便可分伏要害，以待虜至，引使深入，然後擊之，擒之必矣。

translations.literal: When the pasturelands are finished, you may divide forces and lie in wait at critical points for the barbarians to arrive; draw them deep in, then strike—capture is certain.
translations.idiomatic: When the pastures are grazed out, post detachments at the key passes and wait for the enemy; lure them deep, then strike, and capture is certain.

sentences.zh: 涼州路遠，朕不得救。

translations.literal: Liang Province is far; I cannot rescue you.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou is far; I cannot come to your aid.

sentences.zh: 卿若違朕指授，為虜侵害，朕還斬卿。

translations.literal: If you disobey my command and the barbarians harm us, on my return I shall behead you.
translations.idiomatic: Disobey my orders and let the barbarians harm the realm—I will behead you on my return.

sentences.zh: 崔浩、李順為證，非虛言也。

translations.literal: Cui Hao and Li Shun are witnesses—this is no empty word.
translations.idiomatic: Hao and Shun are witnesses; this is no idle threat.

sentences.zh: 」壽頓首受詔。

translations.literal: " Shou kowtowed and received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Shou kowtowed and received the edict — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 壽信卜筮之言，謂賊不來，竟不設備。

translations.literal: Shou trusted the diviners' words that the enemy would not come and in the end made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Shou trusted diviners who said the enemy would not come and made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 而吳提果至，侵及善無，京師大駭。

translations.literal: Wuti indeed arrived, invaded as far as Shanwu, and the capital was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Wuti came as foretold, raided as far as Shanwu, and the capital was thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 壽不知所為，欲築西郭門，請恭宗避保南山。

translations.literal: Shou did not know what to do and wished to build the western outer gate and ask Gongzong to hold Mount Bao in the south for protection.
translations.idiomatic: Shou knew not what to do, proposed sealing the western gate, and asked Gongzong to hold Mount Bao in the south.

sentences.zh: 惠太后不聽，乃止。

translations.literal: Empress Huibao would not listen, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Huibao refused and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 遣司空長孫道生等擊走之。

translations.literal: He sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and others to attack and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Minister of Works Changsun Daosheng and others against them and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 世祖還，以無大損傷，故不追咎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor Shizu returned, because there was no great harm he did not pursue blame.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu returned; as damage was slight he did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 恭宗監國，壽與崔浩等輔政，人皆敬浩，壽獨凌之。

translations.literal: When Gongzong supervised the state Shou with Cui Hao and others assisted in government; all respected Hao, but Shou alone towered over him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongzong supervised the realm Shou assisted government with Cui Hao and others; all honored Hao, but Shou alone looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 又自恃位任，以為人莫己及。

translations.literal: He also relied on his position and office, thinking no one could match him.
translations.idiomatic: He also trusted in rank and office, believing none could equal him.

sentences.zh: 謂其子師曰：「但令吾兒及我，亦足勝人，不須苦教之。

translations.literal: He told his son Shi, "Just let my son and me suffice to surpass others—there is no need to teach him painfully.
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Shi, "Let my son and me alone surpass others—no need to drill him hard.

sentences.zh: 」遇諸父兄弟有如僕隸，夫妻並坐共食，而令諸父餕餘。

translations.literal: " Toward his uncles and brothers he was like toward slaves; husband and wife sat and ate together while he made his uncles eat leftovers.
translations.idiomatic: " He treated uncles and brothers like slaves; he and his wife ate together while making uncles take their leftovers.

sentences.zh: 其自矜無禮如此，為時人所鄙笑。

translations.literal: His arrogant lack of ritual was like this, and people of the time mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mocked him for such arrogant lack of ritual.

sentences.zh: 真君八年薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenjun he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhenjun he died — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant with posthumous title Wenzuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named grand commandant with the title Wenzuan.

sentences.zh: 子平國，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Pingguo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pingguo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 尚城陽長公主，拜駙馬都尉、侍中、中書監，為太子四輔。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Chengyang, was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, Palace Attendant, and Director of the Secretariat, and became one of the crown prince's four tutors.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Chengyang and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law, palace attendant, director of the secretariat, and one of the crown prince's four tutors.

sentences.zh: 正平元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengping he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengping he died — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 子伏干，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Fugan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fugan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 尚濟北公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Jibei and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Jibei and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 和平二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heping he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Heping he died — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 諡曰康。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He received the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no son.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son.

sentences.zh: 伏干弟羆，襲爵。

translations.literal: Fugan's younger brother Pi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Fugan's younger brother Pi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 尚新平長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Xinping and was made Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Xinping and became commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 又除虎牢鎮將，頻以不法致罪。

translations.literal: He was also appointed garrison general of Hulao and repeatedly offended through unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made garrison general of Hulao and repeatedly broke the law.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其勳德之冑，讓而赦之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because he was of a house of old merit and virtue, reproved him and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu, remembering old service, rebuked him and pardoned him each time.

sentences.zh: 轉征東將軍、吐京鎮將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be General Who Campaigns East and commander of the Tujing garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who campaigns east and commander of the Tujing garrison.

sentences.zh: 羆賞善罰惡，深自克勵。

translations.literal: Pi rewarded good and punished evil and strove to discipline himself deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Pi rewarded the good and punished the wicked and applied himself with strict self-discipline.

sentences.zh: 時西河胡叛，羆欲討之，而離石都將郭洛頭拒違不從。

translations.literal: At the time the Hu of Xihe rebelled; Pi wished to punish them, but the capital commandant of Lishi, Guo Luotou, resisted and would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu of Xihe rebelled, Pi wished to strike them, but Lishi commandant Guo Luotou refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 羆遂上表自劾，以威不攝下，請就刑戮。

translations.literal: Pi thereupon submitted a memorial impeaching himself, on the grounds that his authority could not restrain subordinates, and asked to undergo execution.
translations.idiomatic: Pi memorialized to impeach himself, saying his authority could not restrain subordinates, and asked to suffer execution.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃免洛頭官。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu thereupon dismissed Luotou from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu dismissed Luotou from office.

sentences.zh: 山胡劉什婆寇掠郡縣，羆討滅之。

translations.literal: The mountain Hu Liu Shipo raided commanderies and counties; Pi attacked and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain Hu Liu Shipo raided the commanderies; Pi destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 自是部內肅然，莫不敬憚。

translations.literal: From this time within his jurisdiction all was orderly, and none failed to respect and fear him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his district was orderly, and all respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 後改吐京鎮為汾州，仍以羆為刺史。

translations.literal: Later the Tujing garrison was changed to Fenzhou, and Pi was still appointed inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tujing garrison was reorganized as Fenzhou, Pi remained its governor.

sentences.zh: 前吐京太守劉升，在郡甚有威惠，限滿還都，胡民八百餘人詣羆請之。

translations.literal: The former Tujing prefect Liu Sheng had great authority and kindness in the commandery; when his term ended and he returned to the capital, more than eight hundred Hu came to Pi to request him.
translations.idiomatic: Former prefect Liu Sheng had ruled Tujing with authority and kindness; when his term ended and he returned to court, over eight hundred Hu petitioned Pi to bring him back.

sentences.zh: 前定陽令吳平仁亦有恩信，戶增數倍。

translations.literal: The former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren also had grace and trust; registered households increased severalfold.
translations.idiomatic: Former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren likewise won trust, and registered households multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 羆以吏民懷之，並為表請。

translations.literal: Because officials and people cherished them, Pi memorialized to request both.
translations.idiomatic: Pi, seeing how officials and commoners cherished them, memorialized for both appointments.

sentences.zh: 高祖皆從焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu granted each request.

sentences.zh: 羆既頻薦升等，所部守令，咸自砥礪，威化大行，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Since Pi had repeatedly recommended Sheng and the rest, the prefects and magistrates under his jurisdiction all sharpened themselves; awe and transformation spread widely, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's repeated recommendations of Sheng and others spurred every prefect and magistrate under him to sharpen their conduct, and his moral authority transformed the region.

sentences.zh: 州民李軌、郭及祖等七百餘人，詣闕頌羆恩德。

translations.literal: More than seven hundred men of the province, Li Gui and Guo Jizu among them, went to the palace gates to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven hundred provincials, including Li Gui and Guo Jizu, went to the capital to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.

sentences.zh: 高祖以羆政和民悅，增秩延限。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu, because Pi's governance was sound and the people pleased, raised his rank and extended his term.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing sound governance and a content populace, Emperor Gaozu raised Pi's rank and extended his term of office.

sentences.zh: 後徵為光祿勳。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned to be director of the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 隨例降王為魏郡開國公，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: According to precedent his princely title was reduced to Duke Who Founded the State of Weijun with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent his title was reduced to Duke Who Founded the State of Weijun, fief five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又除鎮北將軍、燕州刺史，鎮廣寧。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yan Province, garrisoning Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Yan, garrisoning Guangning.

sentences.zh: 尋遷都督夏州、高平鎮諸軍事，本將軍，夏州刺史，鎮統萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be commander over all military affairs of Xia Province and the Gaoping garrison, with his existing rank, Inspector of Xia Province, garrisoning Tongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made commander of Xia Province and the Gaoping garrison, retained his existing rank, became inspector of Xia, and garrisoned Tongwan.

sentences.zh: 又除侍中、中書監。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made palace attendant and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 穆泰之反，羆與潛通，赦後事發，削封為民。

translations.literal: In Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with him; after an amnesty the matter came out, and his enfeoffment was stripped—he became a registered commoner.
translations.idiomatic: During Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with the plotters; after an amnesty exposed the affair, his fief was revoked and he was reduced to common registration.

sentences.zh: 卒于家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away at home.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，追贈鎮北將軍、恒州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizong he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Heng Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong he was posthumously made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Heng.

sentences.zh: 子建，字晚興，性通率，頗好文史。

translations.literal: His son Jian, courtesy name Wanxing, was open and direct by nature and rather loved literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian, styled Wanxing, was frank by nature and fond of letters.

sentences.zh: 起家祕書郎，稍遷直閤將軍，兼武衞。

translations.literal: He began his career as Secretary of the Palace and was gradually promoted to Direct-palace General and concurrent Defender of the Martial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He began as secretary of the palace, rose to direct-palace general, and served concurrently as defender of the martial guards.

sentences.zh: 建妻尒朱榮之妹，建常依附榮。

translations.literal: Jian's wife was Erzhu Rong's younger sister; Jian often relied on Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's wife was Erzhu Rong's sister; Jian often leaned on Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮入洛之後，除鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、征北將軍，封濟北郡開國公。

translations.literal: After Rong entered Luoyang he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord, General Who Campaigns North, and enfeoffed as Duke Who Founded the State of Jibei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Rong entered Luoyang he was made general who pacifies the east, household grandee with the golden seal and purple cord, general who campaigns north, and duke who founded the state of Jibei commandery.

sentences.zh: 後遷散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、兼尚書、北道行臺、并州事。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Scattered Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Household Grandee, concurrent Master of Writing, Northern Route Mobile Headquarters, and affairs of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became scattered cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, grand general of chariots and cavalry, left household grandee, concurrent master of writing, northern-route mobile headquarters, and overseer of Bing.

sentences.zh: 元曄之立，建兼尚書右僕射，俄轉侍中、驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye was established, Jian was made concurrent Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Rapid Cavalry Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye was enthroned, Jian was made concurrent right vice director of the masters of writing; soon he became palace attendant and rapid-cavalry grand general.

sentences.zh: 出帝末，本將軍、儀同三司、洛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Chu's reign he held his existing rank, Three Excellencies of Honor, and was Inspector of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Chu's reign he held his existing rank, three excellencies of honor, and was inspector of Luo.

sentences.zh: 天平中，坐事自殺於五原城北。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era, for an offense he killed himself north of the city of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianping era he took his own life north of Wuyuan for an offense.

sentences.zh: 子千牙，武定中，開府祭酒。

translations.literal: His son Qianya, in the Wuding era, was libationer of the Bureau that Opens Offices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianya, in the Wuding era, was libationer of the bureau that opens offices.

sentences.zh: 建弟衍，字進興。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Jinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Yan, styled Jinxing.

sentences.zh: 解褐員外郎，封新興縣開國子，稍遷通直常侍，行雲州事。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the russet he was made Outer Palace Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron Who Founded the State of Xinxing county, and gradually promoted to Direct-palace Regular Attendant in charge of Yun Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving the russet he was made outer palace attendant, enfeoffed baron who founded the state of Xinxing county, and rose to direct-palace regular attendant in charge of Yun.

sentences.zh: 羆弟亮，字幼輔，初字老生，早有風度。

translations.literal: Pi's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Youfu, at first styled Laosheng, early showed bearing and style.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's younger brother Liang, styled Youfu, first styled Laosheng, showed refinement and presence from youth.

sentences.zh: 顯祖時，起家為侍御中散。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzu he first entered service as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzu he began his career as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 尚中山長公主，拜駙馬都尉，封趙郡王，加侍中、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, was appointed Commandant of the Imperial Son-in-Law, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao commandery, and given the additional posts Palace Attendant and General Who Campaigns South.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, became commandant of the imperial son-in-law, was enfeoffed prince of Zhao commandery, and named palace attendant and general who campaigns south.

sentences.zh: 徙封長樂王。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Prince of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was transferred to the princedom of Changle.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，除使持節、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession he was made bearer of the staff and inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 在州未期，大著聲稱。

translations.literal: Within the province, before his term was complete, he won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Before his term ended he won great renown in the province.

sentences.zh: 徵為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Master of Writing Within the Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as master of writing within the hall.

sentences.zh: 又遷使持節、征西大將軍、西戎校尉、敦煌鎮都大將。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Bearer of the Staff, General Who Campaigns West, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and Grand General of the Dunhuang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bearer of the staff, general who campaigns west, colonel protector of the western rong, and grand general of the Dunhuang garrison.

sentences.zh: 政尚寬簡，賑恤窮乏。

translations.literal: His government favored leniency and simplicity; he relieved and supported the exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: His rule favored leniency and simplicity; he relieved the poor and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 被徵還朝，百姓追思之。

translations.literal: When he was summoned back to court the common people missed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recalled to court the people missed him.

sentences.zh: 除都督秦梁益三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、領護西戎校尉、仇池鎮將。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander over all military affairs of Qin, Liang, and Yi provinces, General Who Campaigns South, concurrent Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and commander of the Chouchi garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made commander of Qin, Liang, and Yi, general who campaigns south, colonel protector of the western rong, and commander of the Chouchi garrison.

sentences.zh: 時宕昌王梁彌機死，子彌博立，為吐谷渾所逼，來奔仇池。

translations.literal: At the time the King of Dangchang, Liang Miji, died; his son Mibo succeeded, was pressed by Tuyuhun, and came to flee to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Dangchang king Liang Miji died, and his son Mibo succeeded; harried by Tuyuhun, Mibo fled to Chouchi for refuge.

sentences.zh: 亮以彌機蕃欵素著，[2]矜其亡滅；

translations.literal: Liang considered that Miji's long-standing submission to the frontier was well known,[2] and pitied his destruction;
translations.idiomatic: Liang judged that Miji's long submission to the court was well known,[2] and pitied his fall;

sentences.zh: 彌博凶悖，氐羌所棄；

translations.literal: Mibo was violent and perverse, abandoned by the Di and Qiang;
translations.idiomatic: Mibo was violent and perverse and abandoned by the Di and Qiang tribes;

sentences.zh: 彌機兄子彌承，戎民歸樂，表請納之。

translations.literal: Miji's elder brother's son Micheng, whom the tribal peoples gladly followed, memorialized asking to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Miji's nephew Micheng, whom the tribes gladly followed, memorialized asking that he be installed instead.

sentences.zh: 高祖從焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是率騎三萬，次于龍鵠，擊走吐谷渾，立彌承而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led thirty thousand horsemen, halted at Longhu, routed Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then led thirty thousand horse, halted at Longhu, drove off Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，階陵比谷羌董耕奴、斯卑等率眾數千人，寇仇池，屯于陽遐嶺，亮副將楊靈珍率騎擊走之。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang of Jieling Bigu, Dong Gengnu and Si Bei among them, led a multitude of several thousand men, raided Chouchi, and encamped at Yangxia Ridge; Liang's deputy Yang Lingzhen led horsemen and attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Jieling Bigu Qiang, Dong Gengnu and Si Bei among them, led several thousand men against Chouchi and encamped at Yangxia Ridge; Liang's deputy Yang Lingzhen drove them off.

sentences.zh: 氐豪楊卜，自延興以來，從軍征伐，二十一戰，前來鎮將，抑而不聞。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Yang Bu, since Yanxing, had followed the army in campaigns through twenty-one battles; former garrison commanders had suppressed him and never reported his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Bu had fought in twenty-one campaigns since Yanxing, yet successive garrison commanders had suppressed his record and never reported his merit.

sentences.zh: 亮表卜為廣業太守，豪右咸悅，境內大安。

translations.literal: Liang memorialized to make Bu Grand Warden of Guangye; the powerful families were all pleased, and within the borders there was great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Liang memorialized to appoint Bu grand warden of Guangye; local magnates were pleased and the region knew great peace.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be palace attendant and right vice director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: [3]于時，復置司州。

translations.literal: [3] At that time Sizhou was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: [3] At that time Sizhou was re-established — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「司州始立，未有僚吏，須立中正，以定選舉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Sizhou has just been founded and has no staff officers; a Rectifier must be appointed to fix selections.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said, "Sizhou has only just been founded and lacks staff; we must appoint a Rectifier to govern selection.

sentences.zh: 然中正之任，必須德望兼資者。

translations.literal: Yet the Rectifier's post requires both virtue and renown.
translations.idiomatic: That office demands both virtue and public standing.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，崔浩為冀州中正，長孫嵩為司州中正，可謂得人。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—truly men well chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—true examples of the right choice.

sentences.zh: 公卿等宜自相推舉，必令稱允。

translations.literal: You ministers and grandees should deliberate and recommend among yourselves; it must be fitting.
translations.idiomatic: You ministers should deliberate and recommend with care.

sentences.zh: 」尚書陸叡舉亮為司州大中正。

translations.literal: " Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui recommended Liang as Grand Rectifier of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Director Lu Rui recommended Liang as grand rectifier of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時蕭賾遣將陳顯達攻陷醴陽，加亮使持節，征南大將軍，都督懷、洛、南、北豫、徐、兗六州諸軍事以討之。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Ze sent general Chen Xianda to capture Liyang; Liang was given the staff of authority as General Who Campaigns South and commander of military affairs in Huai, Luo, South and North Yu, Xu, and Yan provinces to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Ze sent general Chen Xianda to take Liyang; Liang was given the staff of authority as general who campaigns south and commander of military affairs in Huai, Luo, South and North Yu, Xu, and Yan to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 顯達遁走，乃還。

translations.literal: Xianda fled in flight, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda fled, and Liang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 尋遷司空，參議律令。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Minister of Works and took part in deliberating the code of laws.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made minister of works and helped draft the code of laws.

sentences.zh: 例降爵為公。

translations.literal: By precedent his noble rank was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent his title was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 時文明太后崩，已過期月，高祖毀瘠猶甚。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Wenming had died; more than a month had passed, yet Gaozu was still emaciated from grief.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had died; though more than a month had passed, Gaozu remained wasted with grief.

sentences.zh: 亮表曰：「王者居極，至尊至重，父天母地，懷柔百靈。

translations.literal: Liang submitted a memorial saying: "The king who occupies the apex holds the utmost honor and weight; father is Heaven and mother Earth, cherishing and soothing the hundred spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Liang memorialized: "The ruler at the apex holds supreme honor; father Heaven and mother Earth, he cherishes the hundred spirits.

sentences.zh: 是以古先哲王，制禮成務。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancient sage-kings established rites to complete their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the ancient sage-kings made rites to finish their task.

sentences.zh: 施政立治，必順天而後動；

translations.literal: To set up government and establish order, one must follow Heaven before acting;
translations.idiomatic: To found government and establish order, one must follow Heaven before acting;

sentences.zh: 宣憲垂範，必依典而後行。

translations.literal: to proclaim law and leave example, one must rely on the canon before proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: to proclaim law and leave example, one must rely on the canon before proceeding — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 用能四時不忒，陰陽和暢。

translations.literal: Then the four seasons do not err and yin and yang stay in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Then the four seasons do not err and yin and yang stay in harmony — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 若有過舉，咎徵必集。

translations.literal: If there is excess in conduct, omens of blame will gather.
translations.idiomatic: If conduct goes too far, omens of blame will gather.

sentences.zh: 故大舜至慕，事在納麓之前；

translations.literal: Thus great Shun in utmost filiality acted before he took his place at Mount Lu;
translations.idiomatic: Thus great Shun in utmost filiality acted before he took his place;

sentences.zh: 孔子至聖，喪無過瘠之紀。

translations.literal: Confucius, the utmost sage, left no record of mourning past emaciation.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, the utmost sage, left no record of mourning past emaciation — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 堯書稽古之美，不錄在服之痛；

translations.literal: The Documents of Yao praise antiquity's beauty but do not record the pain of sackcloth;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Yao praise antiquity's beauty but do not record the pain of sackcloth; — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 禮備諸侯之喪，而無天子之式。

translations.literal: the rites complete a feudal lord's mourning yet provide no form for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: the rites complete a feudal lord's mourning yet provide no form for the Son of Heaven — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 雖有上達之言，未見居喪之典。

translations.literal: Though there are lofty words reaching upward, one does not see the canon for occupying mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Though lofty words reach upward, one does not see the canon for occupying mourning.

sentences.zh: 然則位重者為世以屈己，居聖者達命以忘情。

translations.literal: Thus he who is heavy in rank bends himself for the age; he who is sage in station fulfills fate and forgets private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he who is heavy in rank bends himself for the age; he who is sage in station fulfills fate and forgets private feeling — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下至德參二儀，惠澤覃河海，宣禮明刑，動遵古式。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's supreme virtue matches the two principles, your gracious flood reaches river and sea, you spread ritual and clarify punishment, and in motion follow the ancient pattern.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's supreme virtue matches the two principles, your gracious flood reaches river and sea, you spread ritual and clarify punishment, and in motion follow the ancient pattern — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 以至孝之痛，服期年之喪，練事既闋，號慕如始。

translations.literal: Yet with utmost filial grief you wear mourning for a full year; when the second-year observance ended your cries remained as at the start.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with utmost filial grief you wear mourning for a full year; when the second-year observance ended your cries remained as at the start — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 統重極之尊，同眾庶之制，廢越紼之大敬，闕宗祀之舊軌。

translations.literal: You bear the honor of the utmost pole yet share the commoner's rule; you set aside the great reverence of the transition hemp and leave the old track of ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: You bear the honor of the utmost pole yet share the commoner's rule; you set aside the great reverence of the transition hemp and leave the old track of ancestral sacrifice — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 誠由文明太皇太后聖略超古，惠訓深至，欲報之德，昊天罔極，比之前代，戚為過甚。

translations.literal: Truly because Empress Dowager Wenming's sacred design surpassed antiquity and her gracious instruction reached deep, the virtue owed her has no bound in heaven—compared with former ages, your grief is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Truly because Empress Dowager Wenming's sacred design surpassed antiquity and her gracious instruction reached deep, the virtue owed her has no bound in heaven—compared with former ages, your grief is excessive — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 豈所謂順帝之則，約躬隨眾者也。

translations.literal: Is this what is called following the emperor's norm and restraining oneself to follow the multitude?
translations.idiomatic: Is this what is called following the emperor's norm and restraining oneself to follow the multitude? — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 陛下既為天地所子，又為萬民父母。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is both Heaven and Earth's son and the myriad people's parent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is both Heaven and Earth's son and the myriad people's parent — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 子過哀，父則為之慘悴；

translations.literal: If a son mourns past measure, his father is made wretched;
translations.idiomatic: If a son mourns past measure, his father is made wretched; — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 父過戚，子則為之憂傷。

translations.literal: if a father grieves past measure, his son is made sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: if a father grieves past measure, his son is made sorrowful — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 近蒙接見，咫尺旒冕，聖容哀毀，駭感無止，況神祇至靈，而不久虧和氣，微致風旱者哉？

translations.literal: Of late I was granted audience; within a pace of your crown your sacred face was wasted with grief—my shock would not end. How much less will the spirits, utmost in numinous power, long tolerate a slight harm to harmony and a small bringing of wind and drought?
translations.idiomatic: Of late I was granted audience; within a pace of your crown your sacred face was wasted with grief—my shock would not end; How much less will the spirits, utmost in numinous power, long tolerate a slight harm to harmony and a small bringing of wind and drought?

sentences.zh: 書稱『一人有慶，兆民賴之』，今一人過哀，黎元焉繫？

translations.literal: The Documents say, 'When one man has blessing, the myriad look to him.' Now when one man mourns past measure, how are the people anchored?
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, 'When one man has blessing, the myriad look to him.' Now when one man mourns past measure, how are the people anchored? — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 羣官所以顛殞震懼，率土所以危惶悚慄，百姓何仰而不憂，嘉禾何由而播殖。

translations.literal: For this reason the officials are overturned with fear, the realm is shaken with dread, the people have nothing to look up to but worry, and how can the good grain be sown and planted?
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the officials are overturned with fear, the realm is shaken with dread, the people have nothing to look up to but worry, and how can the good grain be sown and planted? — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 願陛下上承金冊遺訓，下稱億兆之心，時襲輕服，數御常膳，修崇郊祠，垂惠咸秩，輿駕時動，以釋憂煩，博採廣諮，以導性氣，息無益之戀，行利見之德；

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty above inherit the golden-book testament, below answer the hundred millions' hearts, at times wear light mourning, often take ordinary meals, restore suburban sacrifice, extend grace throughout the ranks, move the carriage at times to release sorrow, widely consult to guide the temperament, rest from useless longing, and practice the virtue that brings benefit in sight;
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty above inherit the golden-book testament, below answer the hundred millions' hearts, at times wear light mourning, often take ordinary meals, restore suburban sacrifice, extend grace throughout the ranks, move the carriage at times to release sorrow, widely consult to guide the temperament, rest from useless longing, and practice the virtue that brings benefit in sight; — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 則休徵可致，嘉應必臻，禮教並宣，孝慈兼備，普天蒙賴，含生幸甚。

translations.literal: then auspicious omens may be summoned, blessed responses will surely arrive, ritual and teaching will both be proclaimed, filial piety and kindness will both be complete, all under Heaven will receive reliance, and living beings will be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: then auspicious omens may be summoned, blessed responses will surely arrive, ritual and teaching will both be proclaimed, filial piety and kindness will both be complete, all under Heaven will receive reliance, and living beings will be greatly fortunate." — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「苟孝悌之至，無所不通。

translations.literal: An edict said: "If filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing remains blocked.

sentences.zh: 今飄風亢旱，時雨不降，實由誠慕未濃，幽顯無感也。

translations.literal: Now fierce winds and great drought persist and timely rain does not fall—truly because sincere longing is not yet deep and the hidden and manifest are unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fierce winds and drought persist while timely rain withholds itself—because your longing is not yet deep enough for hidden and manifest alike to respond.

sentences.zh: 所言過哀之咎，諒為未衷，省啟以增悲愧。」

translations.literal: What you say of the fault of excessive mourning, I am sure is not the inner truth; reading your memorial only adds grief and shame."
translations.idiomatic: What you call the fault of excessive mourning, I am sure is not your true meaning; reading your memorial only adds grief and shame."

sentences.zh: 尋領太子太傅。

translations.literal: Before long he also held Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also became grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時將建太極殿，引見羣臣於太華殿，高祖曰：「朕仰遵先意，將營殿宇，役夫既至，興功有日。

translations.literal: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, the emperor received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said: "We follow our predecessors' intent and will raise palace halls; the laborers have arrived and the work will begin within days.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, Gaozu received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said: "We follow our predecessors' intent and will raise palace halls; the laborers have arrived and the work will begin within days.

sentences.zh: 今欲徙居永樂，以避囂埃。

translations.literal: We now wish to move to Yongle to escape dust and clamor.
translations.idiomatic: We now wish to move to Yongle to escape dust and clamor — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 土木雖復無心，毀之能不悽愴。

translations.literal: Though in timber and earth I am again without heart, can destroying them fail to wring grief!
translations.idiomatic: Though I am no builder at heart, how can tearing them down fail to wring my heart!

sentences.zh: 今故臨對卿等，與之取別。

translations.literal: We therefore now face you and take leave together.
translations.idiomatic: I have called you here to take leave together.

sentences.zh: 此殿乃高宗所制，爰歷顯祖，逮朕冲年，受位於此。

translations.literal: This hall was made by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here.
translations.idiomatic: This hall was built by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here.

sentences.zh: 但事來奪情，將有改制，仰惟疇昔，惟深悲感。

translations.literal: But affairs seize feeling; there will be a change in design. Looking up to days past, I am only deeply grieved."
translations.idiomatic: But necessity overrides sentiment, and the design must change. Looking back on those days fills me only with grief."

sentences.zh: 」亮稽首對曰：「臣聞稽之卜筮，載自典經，占以決疑，古今攸尚。

translations.literal: Liang bowed his head and replied: "Your subject has heard that consulting divination is recorded in the canonical classics; using it to resolve doubt is honored in ancient and modern times alike.
translations.idiomatic: Liang bowed and replied: "Your subject has heard that consulting divination is recorded in the canonical classics; using it to resolve doubt is honored in ancient and modern times alike.

sentences.zh: 興建之功，事在不易，願陛下訊之蓍龜，以定可否。

translations.literal: The work of construction is not easy to accomplish; I pray Your Majesty consult the milfoil and tortoise to fix whether it may proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The work of construction is not easy to accomplish; I pray Your Majesty consult the milfoil and tortoise to fix whether it may proceed — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 又去歲役作，為功甚多，太廟明堂，一年便就。

translations.literal: Moreover last year's labor projects accomplished very much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall were finished within a year.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover last year's labor had already accomplished much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall were finished within a year.

sentences.zh: 若仍歲頻興，恐民力凋弊。

translations.literal: If works are raised year after year, I fear the people's strength will be carved to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: If works are raised year after year, I fear the people will be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 且材幹新伐，為功不固，願得逾年，小康百姓。

translations.literal: Moreover timber has just been freshly cut and will not stand firm as work; I wish to wait further years and give the people a little ease."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover timber has just been freshly cut and will not stand firm as work; I wish to wait further years and give the people a little ease." — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「若終不為，可如卿言。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "If in the end it is not done, it may be as you say.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "If in the end it is not done, it may be as you say — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 後必為之，逾年何益？

translations.literal: But when it must later be done, what good is waiting another year?"
translations.idiomatic: But when it must later be done, what good is waiting another year?" — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 朕遠覽前王，無不興造。

translations.literal: I have looked far back at former kings—none failed to build.
translations.idiomatic: I have looked far back at former kings, and none failed to build.

sentences.zh: 故有周創業，經建靈臺；

translations.literal: Therefore when Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;

sentences.zh: 洪漢受終，未央是作。

translations.literal: when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was made.
translations.idiomatic: when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was built.

sentences.zh: 草創之初，猶尚若此，況朕承累聖之運，屬太平之基。

translations.literal: At the very founding they were still like this; how much more I, who inherit the fortune of many sages and stand on a foundation of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Even at founding they did as much; how much more should I, inheriting many sages' fortune upon an age of great peace.

sentences.zh: 且今八表清晏，年穀又登，爰及此時，以就大功。

translations.literal: Moreover now the eight directions are clear and calm and the year's grain has again ripened—seize this time to complete the great work.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the eight directions are clear and calm and the year's grain has ripened again—seize this time to complete the great work.

sentences.zh: 人生定分，修短命也，蓍蔡雖智，其如之何。

translations.literal: Man's allotted portion fixes short and long life; though milfoil and tortoise may be wise, what can they do against fate?
translations.idiomatic: A man's allotted span fixes short life or long; milfoil and tortoise may be wise, but what can they do against fate?

sentences.zh: 當委之大分，豈假卜筮。

translations.literal: One must entrust it to the great allotment—how could it depend on divination!"
translations.idiomatic: What fate entrusts does not wait on divination!"

sentences.zh: 」遂移御永樂宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved his residence to Yongle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his residence to Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 後高祖臨朝堂，謂亮曰：「三代之禮，日出視朝，自漢魏已降，禮儀漸殺。

translations.literal: Later, when Gaozu held court in the Hall of Audience, he told Liang: "The rites of the Three Dynasties had the sun rise for audience at court; from Han and Wei downward, ceremony gradually decayed.
translations.idiomatic: Later at the Hall of Audience Gaozu told Liang: "The Three Dynasties held court as the sun rose; from Han and Wei onward ceremony decayed.

sentences.zh: 晉令有朔望集公卿於朝堂而論政事，亦無天子親臨之文。

translations.literal: The Jin ordinance had on the first and fifteenth of the month the gathering of ministers at the Hall of Audience to discuss government, yet there was no text of the Son of Heaven attending in person.
translations.idiomatic: Jin ordinances gathered ministers on the first and fifteenth to discuss government, yet never required the Son of Heaven in person.

sentences.zh: 今因卿等日中之集，中前則卿等自論政事，中後與卿等共議可否。

translations.literal: Now because you gather at midday, before noon you yourselves shall discuss government; after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you gather at midday, before noon you shall discuss government among yourselves; after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done."

sentences.zh: 」遂命讀奏案，高祖親自決之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered memorials read aloud and personally decided them.
translations.idiomatic: He then had memorials read aloud and decided them himself.

sentences.zh: 又謂亮曰：「徐州表給歸化人稟。

translations.literal: He also told Liang: "Xuzhou has memorialized granting grain rations to submitted barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Liang: "Xuzhou has memorialized granting grain rations to submitted barbarians — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 王者民之父母，誠宜許之。

translations.literal: The king is the people's parent; truly it should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: The king is the people's parent; truly it should be granted — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 但今荊揚不賓，書軌未一，方欲親御六師，問罪江介。

translations.literal: But now Jing and Yang are not submissive, the written track is not one; we mean personally to lead the six armies and ask guilt of the Jiang region.
translations.idiomatic: But now Jing and Yang are not submissive, the written track is not one; we mean personally to lead the six armies and ask guilt of the Jiang region — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 計萬戶投化，歲食百萬，若聽其給也，則蕃儲虛竭。

translations.literal: Reckoning ten thousand households submitting, a year's grain would be a million; if we heed granting it, the border stores will be emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Reckoning ten thousand households submitting, a year's grain would be a million; if we heed granting it, the border stores will be emptied — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 雖得戶千萬，猶未成一同。

translations.literal: Though we gain a thousand myriad households, we still have not achieved unity.
translations.idiomatic: Though we gain a thousand myriad households, we still have not achieved unity — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 且欲隨貧賑恤，卿意何如？

translations.literal: For now we wish to follow poverty in relief—what is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: For now we wish to follow poverty in relief—what is your view?" — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 」亮對曰：「所存遠大，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: Liang replied: "What you preserve is far-reaching; it is truly as the sacred edict says."
translations.idiomatic: Liang replied: "What you preserve is far-reaching; it is truly as the sacred edict says." — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 」及車駕南遷，遷武衞大將軍，以本官董攝中軍事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage moved south, he was transferred to Grand General of Martial Guards and, in his existing office, supervised central military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved south he was made grand general of martial guards and, retaining his existing posts, oversaw central military affairs.

sentences.zh: 高祖南伐，以亮錄尚書事，留鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: When Gaozu campaigned south, he put Liang in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left him to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign Gaozu put Liang in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left him to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後高祖將自小平汎舟幸石濟，亮諫曰：「臣聞垂堂之誨，振古成規，於安思危，著於周易。

translations.literal: Later Gaozu from Xiaoping Ford was about to take a boat to Shiji; Liang admonished: "Your subject has heard the teaching of not leaning over the hall's edge—a rule from antiquity to the present; to think of danger in security is set forth in the Book of Changes.
