translations.idiomatic: Later Gaozu was about to take a boat from Xiaoping Ford to Shiji; Liang admonished: "Your subject has heard the teaching of not leaning over the hall's edge—a rule from antiquity to the present; to think of danger in security is set forth in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 是以憑險弗防，沒而不弔。

translations.literal: Therefore relying on peril without guarding ends in drowning without mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore relying on peril without guarding ends in drowning without mourning — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 匹夫之賤，猶不自輕，況萬乘之尊，含生所仰，而可忽乎！

translations.literal: Even a common man's baseness still does not lightly endanger himself; how much more the honor of ten thousand chariots, upon whom living beings rely—can it be neglected!
translations.idiomatic: Even a common man does not lightly endanger himself; how much more the honor of ten thousand chariots, upon whom living beings rely—can it be neglected!

sentences.zh: 是故處則深宮廣廈，行則萬騎千乘。

translations.literal: Hence at rest one dwells in deep palace and broad hall; in motion one has ten thousand riders and a thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Hence at rest one dwells in deep palace and broad hall; in motion one has ten thousand riders and a thousand chariots — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 昔漢帝欲乘舟渡渭，廣德將以首血汙車輪，帝乃感而就橋。

translations.literal: Of old a Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat; Guangde was about to stain the chariot wheels with blood from his head, and the emperor was moved and went to the bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Of old a Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat; Guangde threatened to stain the chariot wheels with his own blood, and the emperor was moved to take the bridge instead.

sentences.zh: 夫一渡小水，猶尚若斯，況洪河浩汗，有不測之慮。

translations.literal: That one crossing of a small stream was still like this; how much more the great river's vast flood, with immeasurable peril!
translations.idiomatic: That one crossing of a small stream was still so perilous; how much more this great river's vast flood, with immeasurable peril!

sentences.zh: 且車乘由人，猶有奔逸致敗之害，況水之緩急，非人所制，脫難出慮表，其如宗廟何！

translations.literal: Moreover the carriage is driven by men, and even so there is the harm of running wild to ruin; how much more the river's slow or swift current, which men do not control—if disaster comes outside all foresight, what of the ancestral temple!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the carriage is driven by men, and even so there is the harm of running wild to ruin; how much more the river's slow or swift current, which men do not control—if disaster comes outside all foresight, what of the ancestral temple! — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「司空言是也。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "The Minister of Works speaks rightly."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "The minister of works is right."

sentences.zh: 及亮兄羆預穆泰反事，亮以府事付司馬慕容契，上表自劾。

translations.literal: When Liang's elder brother Pi was implicated in Mu Tai's rebellion, Liang entrusted his office affairs to the marshal Murong Qi and submitted a memorial impeaching himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's elder brother Pi was implicated in Mu Tai's rebellion, Liang entrusted office affairs to marshal Murong Qi and memorialized to impeach himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖優詔不許，還令攝事。

translations.literal: Gaozu issued a gracious edict and would not permit it, ordering him to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu answered graciously and would not permit it, ordering him to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 亮頻煩固請，久乃許之。

translations.literal: Liang repeatedly and firmly refused; only after long delay was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Liang firmly refused; only after long insistence was permission granted.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、征北大將軍、開府、儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was made bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Campaigns North, with an open office and ceremonial insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made bearer of the staff of authority, general who campaigns north, with an open office and ceremonial insignia equal to the Three Excellencies, and inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 徙封頓丘郡開國公，食邑五百戶，以紹崇爵。

translations.literal: His fief was changed to Duke of Dunqiu with five hundred households, to continue the ennobled line.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to duke of Dunqiu with five hundred households, to continue the ennobled line.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷定州刺史，尋除驃騎大將軍、尚書令，俄轉司空公。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was transferred to Inspector of Ding Province; before long he was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Director of the Masters of Writing, and soon after transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizong's accession he was made inspector of Ding province; before long he was grand general of agile cavalry and director of the Masters of Writing, and soon after minister of works.

sentences.zh: 景明三年薨，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming he died, at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jingming year 3, at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 給東園溫明祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲，錢四十萬、布七百匹、蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: He was given the warm-bright secret coffin of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, four hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the warm-bright secret coffin of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, one suit of clothes, four hundred thousand cash, seven hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 世宗親臨小斂。

translations.literal: Shizong personally attended the lesser obsequies.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong personally attended the lesser obsequies — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉公，領司州牧，諡曰匡。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Grand Commandant and given charge of Sizhou; his posthumous title was Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand commandant and given charge of Sizhou; his posthumous title was Kuang.

sentences.zh: 子紹，字永業。

translations.literal: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 高祖以其貴臣世冑，顧念之。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he was a noble minister's hereditary scion, showed him special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, seeing him a noble minister's hereditary scion, showed him special regard.

sentences.zh: 九歲除員外郎，侍學東宮，轉太子舍人。

translations.literal: At nine he was made Outer Gentleman and attended study in the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to Heir Apparent Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he was made outer gentleman and attended study in the Eastern Palace; he was transferred to heir-apparent attendant.

sentences.zh: 十一尚琅邪長公主，拜駙馬都尉、散騎侍郎，領京兆王愉文學。

translations.literal: At eleven he married the Princess of Langye and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and Literary Tutor to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he married the princess of Langye and was made commandant of the horse guards, regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and literary tutor to Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，通直散騎常侍、高陽王雍友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizong's reign he was Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Companion to Prince of Gaoyang Yong.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizong's accession he was regular attendant of direct communication and companion to Prince of Gaoyang Yong.

sentences.zh: 遭父憂，詔起襲爵，散騎常侍，領主衣都統。

translations.literal: When he met with his father's mourning, an edict ordered him to rise and inherit the title, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and commander of the Masters of the Imperial Wardrobe.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died an edict ordered him to rise from mourning, inherit the title, take regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and command the masters of the imperial wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 遷祕書監、侍中、金紫光祿大夫、光祿卿，又遷衞將軍、太常卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Minister of the Imperial Household; he was again transferred to General of the Guards and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the palace secretariat, attendant-in-ordinary, grand master of the golden seal and purple ribbon, and minister of the imperial household; he was again made general of the guards and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 尋除使持節、都督冀瀛二州諸軍事、本將軍、冀州刺史，以母老固辭，忤旨免官。

translations.literal: Before long he was made bearer of the staff of authority, commander of military affairs in Ji and Ying provinces, in his existing rank as general and as Inspector of Ji Province; because his mother was old he firmly declined, offended the edict, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made bearer of the staff of authority and commander of military affairs in Ji and Ying, retaining his rank as general and inspector of Ji; pleading his mother's age he firmly declined, offended the throne, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 除中書令，轉七兵尚書，徙殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He was made Director of the Secretariat, transferred to Minister of the Seven Arms, and moved to Director of the Palace Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the secretariat, transferred to minister of the seven arms, and moved to director of the palace department.

sentences.zh: 遭所生憂免，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: He met with mourning for his birth mother and was dismissed; in residence for mourning he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When his birth mother died he left office; his mourning conduct won renown for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 又除衞大將軍、左光祿大夫、中書監，復為侍中，領本邑中正。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand General of the Guards, Left Grand Master of the Palace, Director of the Palace Secretariat, again Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned as grand general of the guards, left grand master of the palace, director of the palace secretariat, again attendant-in-ordinary, and rectifier of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹無他才能，而資性方重，罕接賓客，希造人門。

translations.literal: Shao had no other talent, but his nature was square and weighty; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed others' thresholds.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had no special talent, but his nature was square and grave; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed another man's threshold.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉當權熏灼，曾往候紹，紹迎送下階而已，時人歎尚之。

translations.literal: The commander Yuan Cha, when power blazed, once went to Shao's residence; Shao merely met and escorted him down the steps, and men of the time admired and exalted this.
translations.idiomatic: When commander Yuan Cha's power blazed, he once visited Shao's house; Shao merely met him at the gate and saw him down the steps, and contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 及靈太后欲黜叉，猶豫未決，紹贊成之。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated and had not decided, Shao urged approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated, Shao urged her to act.

sentences.zh: 以功加特進，又拜其次子巖為給事中。

translations.literal: For this merit he was given special advancement, and his second son Yan was also appointed Attendant within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he received special advancement, and his second son Yan was made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 尋加儀同三司，領左右。

translations.literal: Soon he was further made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and oversaw the left and right guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was further made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and oversaw the left and right guards — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 時侍中元順與紹同直，順嘗因醉入其寢所。

translations.literal: At that time Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Shun shared duty with Shao; Shun once, drunk, entered his sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Shun shared duty with Shao; once, drunk, he entered Shao's sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 紹擁被而起，正色讓順曰：「身二十年侍中，與卿先君亟連職事，縱卿後進，何宜相排突也！

translations.literal: Shao threw off the quilt and rose, sternly reproaching Shun: "I have been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and with your late father repeatedly held office together; though you are junior in rank, how may you crowd and affront me!
translations.idiomatic: Shao threw off his quilt and rose, sternly reproaching him: "I have been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and served repeatedly with your late father; though you are junior in rank, how dare you crowd and affront me!

sentences.zh: 」遂謝事還家。

translations.literal: " He thereupon resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " He thereupon resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 詔喻久乃起。

translations.literal: Only after an edict admonished him for a long time did he rise.
translations.idiomatic: Only when an edict admonished him for a long time did he return to office.

sentences.zh: 除車騎大將軍、開府、定州刺史，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Opener of the Government, and Inspector of Dingzhou, but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand general of chariots and cavalry, opener of the government, and inspector of Dingzhou, but firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又除侍中，託疾未起。

translations.literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，故得免害。

translations.literal: At the Heyin affair he therefore escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: At the massacre at Heyin he therefore escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 莊帝立，尒朱榮遣人徵之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was established, Erzhu Rong sent men to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned, Erzhu Rong sent men to summon him.

sentences.zh: 紹以為必死，哭辭家廟。

translations.literal: Shao thought he would surely die and wept farewell before the family shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Shao believed he would surely die and wept farewell before the family shrine.

sentences.zh: 及往見榮於邙山，捧手不拜。

translations.literal: When he went to see Rong at Mount Mang, he clasped his hands and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Rong at Mount Mang, he clasped his hands and did not bow.

sentences.zh: 榮亦矯意禮之，顧謂人曰：「穆紹不虛大家兒。

translations.literal: Rong also affected courtesy toward him and, turning to others, said: "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house.
translations.idiomatic: Rong likewise affected courtesy and said to those around him, "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house.

sentences.zh: 」車駕入宮，尋授尚書令、司空公，進爵為王，給班劍四十人，仍加侍中。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage entered the palace, he was soon appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works, advanced to prince, given forty halberds of the imperial guard, and still made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor entered the palace he was soon made director of the masters of writing and minister of works, advanced to prince, granted forty halberds of the imperial guard, and retained Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時河南尹李奬往詣紹。

translations.literal: At that time the Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, went to call on Shao.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Jiang, governor of Henan, went to call on Shao.

sentences.zh: 奬以紹郡民，謂必加敬，紹又恃封邑，是奬國主，待之不為動膝。

translations.literal: Jiang, as a fellow townsman of Shao, thought he would surely receive deference; Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state, and awaited him without rising from his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, as Shao's fellow townsman, expected deference; Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state and sat upright awaiting him without rising.

sentences.zh: 奬憚其位望，致拜而還。

translations.literal: Jiang feared his rank and standing, performed a bow and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang, fearing his rank and standing, bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 議者兩譏焉。

translations.literal: Critics on both sides reproached them.
translations.idiomatic: Observers reproached them both.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之討葛榮也，詔上黨王天穆為前鋒，次於懷縣；

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Prince of Shangdang Tianmu vanguard, halting at Huaixian;
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, an edict made Prince of Shangdang Tianmu vanguard, halting at Huaixian; — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 司徒公楊椿為右軍；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yang Chun was right army;
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yang Chun was right army; — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 紹為後繼。

translations.literal: Shao was rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was rear guard, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 未發，會擒葛榮乃止。

translations.literal: Before they set out, Ge Rong was captured and they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Before they set out, Ge Rong was captured and the march was called off.

sentences.zh: 未幾，降王復本爵。

translations.literal: Before long, the reduced prince was restored to his former noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the reduced prince was restored to his former noble rank.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以紹為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shao was made Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Shao was made inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 行達東郡，顥敗而反。

translations.literal: En route he reached Dongjun; Hao was defeated and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: En route he reached Dongjun; Hao was defeated and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 子長嵩，字子岳。

translations.literal: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changsong, courtesy name Ziyue — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 起家通直郎，再遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He began his career as General of the Palace Library, was twice promoted to Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He began as general of the palace library and was twice promoted to regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，轉鎮東將軍、光祿少卿。

translations.literal: He inherited the title, was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Vice Director of the Household for Imperial Clan Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was transferred to general who pacifies the east and vice director of the household for imperial clan affairs.

sentences.zh: 興和中卒，贈都督冀滄二州諸軍事、征東將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died in the Xinghe era; posthumously made Supervisor of military affairs in Ji and Cang provinces, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Xinghe era and was posthumously made supervisor of military affairs in Ji and Cang provinces, general who pacifies the east, and inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 子巖，武定中，司徒諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His son Yan, in the Wuding era, was Counsellor-Consultant in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan was counsellor-consultant in the ministry of works in the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 平國弟相國，官至安東將軍、濟州刺史、上洛公。

translations.literal: Pingguo's younger brother Xiangguo rose to General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Ji Province, and Duke of Shangluo.
translations.idiomatic: Pingguo's younger brother Xiangguo rose to general who pacifies the east, inspector of Ji Province, and duke of Shangluo.

sentences.zh: 相國弟正國，尚長樂公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Xiangguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangguo's younger brother Zhengguo married the Princess of Changle and was made commandant of the horse guards.

sentences.zh: 子平城，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Pingcheng died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pingcheng died young — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，始平公主薨於宮，追贈平城駙馬都尉，與公主合葬。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made Commandant of the Horse Guards and granted a posthumous marriage burial with the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen, when the Princess of Shiping died in the palace, Pingcheng was posthumously made commandant of the horse guards and given a posthumous marriage burial with her.

sentences.zh: 平城弟長城，司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Pingcheng's younger brother Changcheng was Left Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Pingcheng's younger brother Changcheng was left chief clerk in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 子世恭，武定中，朱衣直閤。

translations.literal: His son Shigong, in the Wuding era, was Supervisor of the Red-Robed Palace Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shigong was supervisor of the red-robed palace attendants in the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 長城弟彧，符璽郎中。

translations.literal: Changcheng's younger brother Yu was Attendant of the Seals.
translations.idiomatic: Changcheng's younger brother Yu was attendant of the seals.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子永延，尚書騎兵郎、青州征東司馬。

translations.literal: His son Yongyan was Cavalry Officer in the Ministry of Writing and eastern campaign marshal of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongyan was cavalry officer in the ministry of writing and eastern campaign marshal of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 正國弟應國，征西將軍、張掖公。

translations.literal: Zhengguo's younger brother Yingguo was General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengguo's younger brother Yingguo was general who pacifies the west and duke of Zhangye.

sentences.zh: 子度孤，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Dugu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dugu succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 平南將軍、梁城鎮將。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the South and garrison commander of Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was general who pacifies the south and garrison commander of Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 子清休，頗有將略。

translations.literal: His son Qingxiu had considerable military talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingxiu had considerable military talent — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 司農少卿、武衞將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Imperial Granaries, General of the Martial Guard, and Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice director of the imperial granaries, general of the martial guard, and grand master of brilliant happiness.

sentences.zh: 出為驃騎大將軍、夏州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as grand general of agile cavalry and inspector of Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 子鐵槌，祕書郎。

translations.literal: His son Tiechui was Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tiechui was secretary.

sentences.zh: 應國弟安國，歷金部長、殿中尚書，加右衞將軍，賜爵新平子。

translations.literal: Yingguo's younger brother Anguo successively held Director of the Gold Section and Director of the Palace Secretariat, was added General of the Right Guard, and granted the title Marquis of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Yingguo's younger brother Anguo served in turn as director of the gold section and director of the palace secretariat, was added general of the right guard, and enfeoffed as marquis of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 為乙渾所殺，追贈征虜 674 將軍。

translations.literal: He was killed by Yihun; posthumously made [674] General Who Subdues the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by Yihun and posthumously made general who subdues the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 子吐萬，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tuman inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuman succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 襄城鎮將。

translations.literal: Garrison commander of Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was garrison commander of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 子金寶，祕書郎。

translations.literal: His son Jinbao was Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jinbao was secretary.

sentences.zh: 壽弟伏真，高宗世，稍遷尚書，賜爵任城侯。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother Fuzhen, in Emperor Wencheng's time, was gradually promoted to Director of the Secretariat and granted the title Marquis of Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother Fuzhen, under Emperor Wencheng, was gradually promoted to director of the secretariat and enfeoffed as marquis of Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 出為兗州刺史、假寧東將軍、濮陽公。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Yan Province, acting General Who Pacifies the East, and Duke of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as inspector of Yan Province, acting general who pacifies the east, and duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 子常貴，南陽太守。

translations.literal: His son Changgui was Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changgui was administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 伏真弟多侯，歷位殿中給事、左將軍，賜爵長寧子。

translations.literal: Fuzhen's younger brother Duohou held in succession Attendant within the Palace Hall, General of the Left, and was granted the title Marquis of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhen's younger brother Duohou served in turn as attendant within the palace hall and general of the left, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Changning.

sentences.zh: 遷司衞監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to supervisor of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，乙渾專權。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yihun monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng died, Yihun monopolized power — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 時司徒陸麗在代郡溫湯療病，渾忌之，遣多侯追麗。

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Works Lu Li was treating illness at hot springs in Dai Commandery; Hun envied him and sent Duohou to pursue Li.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Lu Li was then taking the waters for illness in Dai Commandery; Hun envied him and sent Duohou to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 多侯謂麗曰：「渾有無君之心，大王眾所望也，去必危，宜徐歸而圖之。

translations.literal: Duohou told Li: "Hun has a heart that disowns his lord; Your Highness is what the masses look to; if you go you will surely be in peril; you should return slowly and plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Duohou told him, "Hun harbors treason against his sovereign. Your Highness is whom the realm looks to; if you go you will surely be in peril. Return slowly and plot against him.

sentences.zh: 」麗不從，遂為渾所害，多侯亦見殺。

translations.literal: " Li did not follow and was thereupon killed by Hun; Duohou was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Li did not listen and was killed by Hun; Duohou was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 諡曰烈。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Lie.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title Lie (Fierce).

sentences.zh: 子胡兒襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Hu'er inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hu'er succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 觀弟翰，平原鎮將、西海王。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and Prince of Xihai.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Han was garrison commander of Pingyuan and prince of Xihai.

sentences.zh: 薨。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子龍仁，襲爵，降為公。

translations.literal: His son Longren inherited the title and was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Longren succeeded him the title and was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子豐國，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Fengguo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fengguo succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 豐國弟子弼，有風格，善自位置。

translations.literal: Fengguo's nephew Bi had style and knew how to place himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fengguo's nephew Bi had style and presence and knew his place.

sentences.zh: 涉獵經史，與長孫稚、陸希道等齊名於世，矜己陵物，頗以損焉。

translations.literal: He ranged through the classics and histories and was famed with Changsun Zhi, Lu Xidao, and others; he prized himself and looked down on others, and lost ground by this.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through the classics and histories and stood equal in renown with Changsun Zhi, Lu Xidao, and others, yet he prized himself and looked down on others and suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 高祖初定氏族，欲以弼為國子助教。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen at the beginning fixed the clans, he wished to make Bi Assistant Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen at the beginning fixed the clans, he wished to make Bi assistant director of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 弼辭曰：「先臣以來，蒙恩累世，比校徒流，實用慚屈。

translations.literal: Bi declined, saying: "From my forefathers on we have received favor generation after generation; compared with the student officials, this would truly humble me in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Bi declined, saying, "From my forefathers on we have received favor generation after generation; compared with the student officials, this would truly humble me in shame.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「朕欲敦厲冑子，故屈卿光之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I wish to encourage and exhort the sons of the nobility; therefore I humble you to go first and shine there.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I wish to encourage the sons of the nobility; therefore I humble you to go first and shine there.

sentences.zh: [4]白玉投泥，豈能相污？

translations.literal: [4] White jade cast in mud—how can it be stained?"
translations.idiomatic: [4] "White jade cast in mud cannot be stained!"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「既遇明時，耻沉泥滓。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Having met a bright age, I would be ashamed to sink in the mire.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "In a bright age I would be ashamed to sink in the mire.

sentences.zh: 」會司州牧、咸陽王禧入，高祖謂禧曰：「朕與卿作州都，舉一主簿。

translations.literal: " It happened that the Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered; the emperor said to Xi: "I make you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: " Just then Prince of Xianyang Wang Xi entered; the emperor said to Xi, "I make you and the prince provincial overseers; choose one chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 」即命弼謁之。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately ordered Bi to pay his respects to the prince.

sentences.zh: 因為高祖所知。

translations.literal: Thus he came to the emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he came to the emperor's notice — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 輿駕南征，特敕隨從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, a special edict ordered him to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south, a special edict ordered him to follow.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除尚書郎，以選為廣平王懷國郎中令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Director in the Masters of Writing and, by selection, Director of the Household of Prince of Guangping Huai.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made director in the masters of writing and, by selection, director of the household of Prince of Guangping Huai.

sentences.zh: [5]數有匡諫之益。

translations.literal: [5] He often had the benefit of corrective admonition.
translations.idiomatic: [5] He often offered useful corrective counsel.

sentences.zh: 世宗善之。

translations.literal: The emperor favored him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored him, the annals record.

sentences.zh: 除中書舍人，轉司州治中、別駕，歷任有稱。

translations.literal: He was made Palace Secretariat Attendant, transferred to Administrator of the Secretariat of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Director, and in successive posts had a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace secretariat attendant, transferred to administrator of the secretariat of the department of state affairs and vice director, and earned a reputation in successive posts.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，河州羌却鐵怱反，[6]敕兼黃門，慰喻怱。

translations.literal: In Suzong's time, the Qiang of Hezhou, Que Tiecong, rebelled; [6] he was ordered concurrently as Yellow Gate Attendant to console and persuade Tiecong.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong, when the Qiang of Hezhou, Que Tiecong, rebelled, [6] he was ordered concurrently as yellow gate attendant to console and persuade Tiecong.

sentences.zh: 以功加前將軍，賜以錢帛。

translations.literal: For merit he was added General of the Vanguard and granted money and silks.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was added general of the vanguard and granted money and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋以本將軍行揚州事，追拜平西將軍、華州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon with his original rank as general he administered Yang Province affairs; he was then advanced to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with his former rank as general, he administered Yang Province; he was then advanced to general who pacifies the west and inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，時年五十一。

translations.literal: He died in the province, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、征北將軍、定州刺史，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Dingzhou; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made bearer of the staff, general who pacifies the north, and inspector of Dingzhou, with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 子季齊，釋褐司徒參軍事、開府騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Jiqi, on first leaving the sack, was Clerk in the Ministry of Works and cavalry officer in the opening office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiqi, on first entering service, was clerk in the ministry of works and cavalry officer in the opening office.

sentences.zh: 翰弟顗，忠謹有材力。

translations.literal: Han's younger brother Yan was loyal, careful, and had strength and talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han's younger brother Yan was loyal, careful, and had strength and talent — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 太宗時為中散，轉侍御郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mingyuan's time he was Attendant Censor, transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan he was attendant censor, then attendant of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 從世祖征赫連昌，勇冠一時，世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Taiwu in the campaign against Helian Chang; his bravery led the age; Emperor Taiwu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Taiwu against Helian Chang; his bravery led the age, and Taiwu praised him.

sentences.zh: 遷侍輦郎、殿中將軍，賜爵泥陽子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage and General in the Palace Hall, granted the title Marquis of Niyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant of the imperial carriage and general in the palace hall and enfeoffed as marquis of Niyang.

sentences.zh: 從征和龍，功超諸將，拜司衞監，加龍驤將軍，進爵長樂侯。

translations.literal: He followed the expedition against Helong; his merit surpassed the generals; he was made Supervisor of the Palace Guards, added General of Agile Cavalry, and advanced to Marquis of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the expedition against Helong; his merit surpassed the other generals; he was made supervisor of the palace guards, added general of agile cavalry, and advanced to marquis of Changle.

sentences.zh: 曾從世祖田於崞山，有虎突出，顗搏而獲之。

translations.literal: Once he followed the emperor hunting at Mount Guo; a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Once, following the emperor hunting at Mount Guo, a tiger burst out and Yan wrestled it down.

sentences.zh: 世祖歎曰：「詩所謂『有力如虎』，顗乃過之。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed: "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "The Odes say, 'Strong as a tiger'—Yan surpasses even that!

sentences.zh: 」後從駕西征白龍，北討蠕蠕，以功加散騎常侍、鎮北將軍，進爵建安公。

translations.literal: " Later he followed the carriage west against Bailong and north to punish the Rouran; for merit he was added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and General Who Pacifies the North, and advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: " He later followed campaigns west against Bailong and north against the Rouran; for merit he was added regular attendant of scattered cavalry and general who pacifies the north, and advanced to duke of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 出為北鎮都將，徵拜殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He went out as commander of the northern garrison, was summoned and made Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as commander of the northern garrison, was summoned, and made director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出鎮涼州，所在著稱。

translations.literal: He went out to garrison Liangzhou and was famed wherever he served.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to garrison Liangzhou and won renown wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 還加散騎常侍，領太倉尚書。

translations.literal: On his return he was added Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and concurrent Director of the Imperial Granary.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was added regular attendant of scattered cavalry and concurrent director of the imperial granary.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，為征西大將軍、督諸軍事，西征吐谷渾，出南道。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wencheng's time he was General Who Pacifies the West and supervised all military affairs in the western campaign against Tuyuhun, taking the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wencheng he was general who pacifies the west, supervised all military affairs in the western campaign against Tuyuhun, and took the southern route.

sentences.zh: 坐擊賊不進，免官爵徙邊。

translations.literal: For striking the bandits without advancing, he was stripped of office and rank and banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Because he failed to press the attack, he was stripped of office and rank and sent to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 高祖又以顗著勳前朝，徵為內都大官。

translations.literal: Gaozu again, because Yi had shown merit in the former dynasty, summoned him as Grand Inner Custodian.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, remembering Yi's merit under the former emperor, recalled him as grand inner custodian.

sentences.zh: 天安元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tian'an he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tian'an year 1.

sentences.zh: 贈征西大將軍、建安王，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns West and Prince of Jian'an; posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who campaigns west and prince of Jian'an, with the posthumous title Kang.

sentences.zh: 子寄生，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jisheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jisheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 寄生弟栗，涼州鎮將、安南公。

translations.literal: Jisheng's younger brother Li, Liangzhou garrison commander and Duke Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Jisheng's brother Li was Liangzhou garrison commander and duke who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 子祁，字願德。

translations.literal: His son Qi, courtesy name Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qi, styled Yuande.

sentences.zh: 通直常侍、上谷河內二郡太守、司州治中、太子右衞率。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, Administrator of Shanggu and Hanoi commanderies, Secretariat Aide of Si Province, Crown Prince Right Guard Leader.
translations.idiomatic: He served as regular attendant of direct communication, administrator of Shanggu and Hanoi, secretariat aide of Si Province, and crown prince right guard leader.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子景相，字霸都。

translations.literal: His son Jingxiang, courtesy name Badu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxiang, styled Badu.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人、上黨太守。

translations.literal: Secretariat Attendant, Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretariat attendant and administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 栗弟泥乾，為羽林中郎，賜爵臨安男。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Nigan, held Central Protocol Regiment lieutenant and was granted the title Baron of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Li's brother Nigan was a central protocol regiment lieutenant and was enfeoffed baron of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 後稍歷顯職，除冀州刺史，假安南將軍、鉅鹿公。

translations.literal: Later he gradually held eminent posts; made Inspector of Ji Province, acting General Who Pacifies the South and Duke of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose through eminent posts, became inspector of Ji Province, and held acting rank as general who pacifies the south and duke of Julu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子渾，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Hun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hun succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 祕書中散。

translations.literal: Secretariat Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: He was secretariat archivist.

sentences.zh: 子令宣，通直常侍。

translations.literal: His son Lingxuan, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lingxuan was regular attendant of direct communication.

sentences.zh: 崇宗人醜善，太祖初，率部歸附，與崇同心勠力，禦侮左右。

translations.literal: Chong's clansman Chou Shan, at the beginning of Taizu, led his division in submission and, with Chong, joined hearts and shared strength to defend left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's clansman Chou Shan, in Taizu's early reign, led his following in to submit and, with Chong, fought side by side at the ruler's left and right.

sentences.zh: 從征窟咄、劉顯，破平之。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against Kuduo and Liu Xian and defeated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaigns against Kuduo and Liu Xian and broke and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 又從擊賀蘭部，平庫莫奚。

translations.literal: He also followed in striking the Helan tribe and pacified the Kumoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed in attacking the Helan and pacified the Kumoxi.

sentences.zh: 拜天部大人，居於東蕃。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division and dwelt in the eastern quarter.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grandee of the heavenly division and dwelt in the eastern quarter.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子莫提，從平中原，為中山太守。

translations.literal: His son Moti, following in pacifying the Central Plains, was Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Moti, after helping pacify the central plains, was administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 除寧南將軍、相州刺史，假陽陵侯。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Xiangzhou, acting Marquis of Yangling.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general who pacifies the south and inspector of Xiangzhou, with acting rank as marquis of Yangling.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子吐，太宗世，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His son Tu, in Taizong's time, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tu was regular attendant of scattered cavalry under Taizong.

sentences.zh: 卒於侍中、鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: He died while holding Palace Attendant and General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as palace attendant and general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 子敦，輔國將軍、西部都將。

translations.literal: His son Dun, General Who Assists the State and Western Frontier Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dun was general who assists the state and western frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 賜爵富平子。

translations.literal: He was granted the title Viscount of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed viscount of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子純，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 歷散騎常侍、光祿勳。

translations.literal: He served as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and Director of the Palace Residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was regular attendant of scattered cavalry and director of the palace residence.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，右衞將軍，尋除右將軍、河州刺史。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time he was Right Guard General; shortly made Right General and Inspector of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he was right guard general, then right general and inspector of He Province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮北將軍、并州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made general who pacifies the north and inspector of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 子盛，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Sheng inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng succeeded him the title.

sentences.zh: 直閤將軍。

translations.literal: Direct-Palace General.
translations.idiomatic: He was direct-palace general.

sentences.zh: 盛弟裕，輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Sheng's younger brother Yu, General Who Assists the State and Palace Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's brother Yu was general who assists the state and palace scribe.

sentences.zh: 裕子禮，東牟太守。

translations.literal: Yu's son Li, Administrator of Dongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Li was administrator of Dongmou.

sentences.zh: 禮弟略，武定末，魏尹丞。

translations.literal: Li's younger brother Lue, at the end of Wuding, Vice Director of the capital Intendant's office.
translations.idiomatic: Li's brother Lue, at the end of Wuding, was vice director under the capital intendant.

sentences.zh: 純弟鑖，歷東宮庶子、汲郡太守。

translations.literal: Chun's younger brother Sa, served as Eastern Palace Vice Prefect and Administrator of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's brother Sa was eastern palace vice prefect and administrator of Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，為懷朔鎮將，東、北中郎將，豳、幽、涼三州刺史。

translations.literal: In Shizong's time he was made Garrison Commander of Huaishuo, Eastern and Northern Central Commander, and Inspector of Bin, You, and Liang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizong he was garrison commander of Huaishuo, eastern and northern central commander, and inspector of Bin, You, and Liang provinces.

sentences.zh: 肅宗世，除平北將軍、并州刺史、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Suzong's time he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Bing Province, and Grandee of the Golden Crown and Purple Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Suzong he was made general who pacifies the north, inspector of Bing Province, and grandee of the golden crown and purple radiance.

sentences.zh: 在公以威猛見稱。

translations.literal: In office he was famed for fierce might.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was famed for fierce might — so the record runs.

sentences.zh: 卒時年七十四，贈散騎常侍、征東將軍、相州刺史，諡曰安。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-four; posthumously made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, General Who Campaigns East, Inspector of Xiangzhou; posthumous title An.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four and was posthumously made regular attendant of scattered cavalry, general who campaigns east, and inspector of Xiangzhou, with the posthumous title An.

sentences.zh: 子顯壽，長水校尉。

translations.literal: His son Xianshou, Colonel of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianshou was colonel of the long river.

sentences.zh: 顯壽弟顯業，卒於散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Xianshou's younger brother Xianye died while holding Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Xianshou's brother Xianye died as regular attendant of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 子琳弟良，字先德。

translations.literal: Zilin's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Zilin's younger brother Liang, styled Xiande.

sentences.zh: 司空行參軍、將作丞、司徒祭酒、安東將軍、南鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: Bureau Aide in the Directorate of Works, Director of Palace Construction, Libationer of the Masters of Writing, General Who Pacifies the East, Administrator of Southern Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was directorate of works bureau aide, director of palace construction, libationer of the masters of writing, general who pacifies the east, and administrator of southern Julu.

sentences.zh: 頗有民譽。

translations.literal: He had considerable repute among the people.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed considerable repute among the people.

sentences.zh: 入為司徒司馬、大將軍從事中郎、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He entered service as Masters of Writing Marshal, Staff Supervisor of the Grand General, and Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as masters of writing marshal, staff supervisor of the grand general, and secretariat attendant.

sentences.zh: 武定六年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wuding year 6.

sentences.zh: 贈征東將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously made General Who Campaigns East and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made general who campaigns east and inspector of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：穆崇夙奉龍顏，早著誠節，遂膺寵眷，位極台鼎；

translations.literal: The historiographer writes: From of old Mu Chong served the dragon countenance, early showed loyal devotion, and so received favor to the summit of the secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Mu Chong long served the throne, showed early loyalty, and rose to the secretariat's peak;

sentences.zh: 至乃身豫逆謀，卒蒙全護，明主之於勞臣，不亦厚矣！

translations.literal: he even took part in treasonous plotting yet in the end was wholly spared — how thick is an enlightened lord's treatment of his toiling servants!
translations.idiomatic: he even joined treason yet was spared in the end — how generous is an enlightened ruler toward a weary servant!

sentences.zh: 從享廟庭，抑亦尚功之義。

translations.literal: To share sacrifice in the temple court also honored the principle of valuing merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sharing the temple sacrifice likewise honored merit above all.

sentences.zh: 觀少當公輔之任，業器其優乎？

translations.literal: Guan in youth was fit for ministerial office — were his talents and capacity not outstanding?
translations.idiomatic: Guan in youth was fit for the highest offices — were his talent and bearing not outstanding?

sentences.zh: 顗壯烈顯達，亮寬厚致位，紹立虛簡之操，弼有風格之名，世載不隕，青紫兼列，盛矣。

translations.literal: Yi was fierce and illustrious; Liang reached rank through generous breadth; Shao upheld unadorned simplicity; Bi bore a name for style — generation on generation they did not fall, purple and blue offices filling the rolls — how grand!
translations.idiomatic: Yi blazed with martial fame; Liang rose through generous breadth; Shao kept unadorned simplicity; Bi won a name for style — generation after generation the house did not decline, purple and blue rank filling the rolls — how grand!

sentences.zh: 至於壽以貴終，羆止削廢，人之無禮，為幸蓋多。

translations.literal: As for Shou, he ended in wealth and rank; Pi alone was stripped and reduced — men's lack of propriety makes good fortune all the more common.
translations.idiomatic: Shou died in wealth and rank; Pi alone was stripped and reduced — when men abandon propriety, luck counts for more.

sentences.zh: 醜之子孫，不乏名位，亦有人哉！

translations.literal: Chou's descendants too were not lacking in fame and rank — they also had their men!
translations.idiomatic: Chou's descendants too held name and rank — the line also had its men!

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 崇外甥于桓等謀執太祖以應之 諸本及北史卷二０穆崇傳「桓」都作「植」。

translations.literal: "Chong's nephew Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu to respond": in various editions and Beishi juan 20, Biography of Mu Chong, "Huan" all reads "Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: "Chong's nephew Yu Huan and others plotted to seize Taizu to join them": editions and Beishi juan 20, Mu Chong's life, all read Huan  as Zhi .

sentences.zh: 冊府卷一三四

translations.literal: Cefu juan 134
translations.idiomatic: Cefu, juan 134

sentences.zh: 〈一六一六頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 1616〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 1616

sentences.zh: 作「桓」。

translations.literal: reads "Huan."
translations.idiomatic: has "Huan."

sentences.zh: 按卷二太祖紀記此事百衲本、南本作「桓」，他本作「植」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Juan 2, Annals of Taizu, recording this affair, has the patchwork and Southern editions reading "Huan" and other editions reading "Zhi."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Taizu's annals, juan 2, on this affair have patchwork and Southern texts with Huan and other editions with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 北史卷一魏紀一、本書及北史卷一五窟咄傳作「桓」。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 1, Annals of Wei 1, this book, and Beishi juan 15, Biography of Kuduo, all read "Huan."
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 1 (Wei annals 1), this book, and Beishi juan 15 (Kuduo) all have Huan.

sentences.zh: 冊府此條採自穆崇傳，却也作「桓」。

translations.literal: This Cefu entry was taken from the Mu Chong biography, yet it too reads "Huan."
translations.idiomatic: This Cefu entry comes from Mu Chong's life yet also reads Huan.

sentences.zh: 知「植」字訛，今據冊府改。

translations.literal: Knowing the character "Zhi" is erroneous, the text is now emended according to Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi is a corruption; the text is emended per Cefu.

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: The same below.
translations.idiomatic: The same below; not listed again.

sentences.zh: 蕃欵素著 諸本「欵」作「教」。

translations.literal: "As a frontier subject his loyal submission was long manifest": in various editions "kuan" (submission) reads "jiao" (teach).
translations.idiomatic: "As a frontier subject his loyal submission was long manifest": editions read kuan (submission) as jiao (teach).

sentences.zh: 冊府卷三五三

translations.literal: Cefu juan 353
translations.idiomatic: Cefu, juan 353

sentences.zh: 〈四一九二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 4192〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 4192

sentences.zh: 作「欵」。

translations.literal: reads "kuan."
translations.idiomatic: has "kuan" (submission).

sentences.zh: 按「欵」是「欵服」「誠欵」之意，意謂作為「藩臣」的「忠誠」態度素著，「教」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Commentary: "kuan" means "kuanfu" (submission) and "chengkuan" (sincere submission) — that is, as a "frontier subject" his "loyal" attitude was long manifest; the character "jiao" is erroneous and is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: kuan means loyal submission as a frontier subject; jiao is a corruption and is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中尚書右僕射 北史卷二０「右」作「左」。

translations.literal: "Summoned as Palace Attendant and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing": Beishi juan 20 has "right" as "left."
translations.idiomatic: "Summoned as palace attendant and right vice director of the masters of writing": Northern History juan 20 reads right as left.

sentences.zh: 按卷七上高祖紀太和十二年四月、十二月並見「左僕射穆亮」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Juan 7, upper, Annals of Gaozu, fourth month of the twelfth year of Taihe and twelfth month both record "Left Vice Director Mu Liang."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Gaozu's annals, juan 7 upper, Taihe year 12, months 4 and 12, both record "left vice director Mu Liang."

sentences.zh: 疑作「左」是。

translations.literal: It is suspected that "left" is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Left is likely correct.

sentences.zh: 故屈卿光之 南、北、殿、局四本「光」作「先」，百衲本、汲本作「光」。

translations.literal: "Therefore I humble you to bring glory to it": in the Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau four editions "guang" (glory) reads "xian" (before); the patchwork and Ji editions read "guang."
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore I humble you to bring glory to it": Southern, Northern, Palace, and Bureau editions read guang (glory) as xian (before); patchwork and Ji have guang.

sentences.zh: 按這是說穆觀當國子助教，於此官有光，今從百衲本。

translations.literal: Commentary: This says Mu Guan was to be national university assistant; in that office there was glory — now follow the patchwork edition.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Mu Guan was to be national university assistant, an office that brought honor; the patchwork reading is followed.

sentences.zh: 以選為廣平王懷國郎中令 諸本「廣」作「高」，北史卷二０作「廣」。

translations.literal: "Selected as Kingdom Chamberlain for Prince of Guangping Huai": in various editions "Guang" reads "Gao"; Beishi juan 20 reads "Guang."
translations.idiomatic: "Selected as kingdom chamberlain for Prince of Guangping Huai": editions read Guang  as Gao ; Northern History juan 20 has Guang.

sentences.zh: 按廣平王懷，本書卷二二、北史卷一九有傳，「高」字顯訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Commentary: Prince of Guangping Huai has biographies in this book juan 22 and Beishi juan 19; the character "Gao" is clearly erroneous and is now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Prince of Guangping Huai has lives in this book juan 22 and Beishi juan 19; Gao is clearly wrong and is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 河州羌却鐵怱反 諸本「怱」作「忽」，卷九肅宗紀神龜元年、卷一０五之四天象志四記此事作「怱」。

translations.literal: "The Qiang of He Province, Que Tiecong, rebelled": in various editions "cong" reads "hu"; juan 9, Annals of Suzong, first year of Shengui, and juan 105, part 4, Monograph on Astronomy 4, recording this affair, all read "cong."
translations.idiomatic: "The Qiang of He Province, Que Tiecong, rebelled": editions read cong  as hu ; Suzong annals juan 9, Shengui year 1, and Astronomy monograph juan 105.4 all have cong.

sentences.zh: 卷四一源賀附源子恭傳作「忽」，而北史卷二八源子恭傳作「怱」。

translations.literal: Juan 41, Biography of Yuan He with attached Biography of Yuan Zigong, reads "hu," while Beishi juan 28, Biography of Yuan Zigong, reads "cong."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 41, Yuan He with attached Yuan Zigong, has hu; Beishi juan 28, Yuan Zigong, has cong.

sentences.zh: 按却鐵怱乃羌人名。

translations.literal: Commentary: Que Tiecong was a Qiang personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Que Tiecong was a Qiang man's name.

sentences.zh: 周書三朝本屢見「傍乞鐵怱」，殿本也常訛作「忽」。

translations.literal: The Zhou shu three-dynasty edition repeatedly has "Pangqi Tiecong," and the Palace edition also often corrupts it to "hu."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou shu three-dynasty text repeatedly has "Pangqi Tiecong," and the Palace edition also often corrupts this to hu.

sentences.zh: 今據紀改。

translations.literal: Now emended according to the annals.
translations.idiomatic: Emended per the annals.

sentences.zh: 阿至羅國主副羅越居為蠕蠕所破 百衲本「阿」作「河」，他本作「何」，冊府卷七二八

translations.literal: "The lord of the Azhi Luo state, Fuluo Yueju, was broken by the Rouran": the patchwork edition reads "A" as "He," other editions as "He," Cefu juan 728
translations.idiomatic: "The Azhi Luo lord Fuluo Yueju was broken by the Rouran": patchwork reads A  as He ; other editions as He ; Cefu juan 728

sentences.zh: 〈八六六０頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 8660〉
translations.idiomatic: folio 8660

sentences.zh: 作「阿」。

translations.literal: reads "A."
translations.idiomatic: has "A" (Azhi).

sentences.zh: 按北史卷六齊紀上，北齊書卷一神武紀上

translations.literal: Commentary: Beishi juan 6, Annals of Qi, upper, Beishi juan 1, Annals of Divine Martiality, upper
translations.idiomatic: Note: Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, upper), Beishi juan 1 (Divine Martiality, upper)

translations.literal: 〈supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: supplement

sentences.zh: 永熙二年、卷二神武紀下

translations.literal: Yongxi year 2, and juan 2, Annals of Divine Martiality, lower
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi year 2, and juan 2 (Divine Martiality, lower)

translations.literal: 〈supplement〉
translations.idiomatic: supplement

sentences.zh: 武定三年並見「阿至羅」，今據冊府改。

translations.literal: Wuding year 3 all record "Azhi Luo"; now emended according to Cefu.
translations.idiomatic: Wuding year 3 all have "Azhi Luo"; emended per Cefu.
